'''Doug Jones''' (born May 24, 1960) is an American actor, [[contortion]]ist, and [[mime artist]]. He is best known for portraying [[non-human]] [[Creature actor|creatures]], usually via heavy make-up and visual effects. He is well known for his collaborations with acclaimed filmmaker [[Guillermo del Toro]], most notably as [[Abe Sapien]] in ''[[Hellboy (2004 film)|Hellboy]]'' (2004) and its [[Hellboy II: The Golden Army|2008 sequel]], the Faun and the Pale Man in ''[[Pan's Labyrinth]]'' (2006), and the Amphibian Man in ''[[The Shape of Water]]'' (2017).

Jones' other film credits include ''[[Hocus Pocus (1993 film)|Hocus Pocus]]'' (1993) and its 2022 sequel, ''[[Hocus Pocus 2]]'';  ''[[Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer]]'' (2007); ''[[Absentia (film)|Absentia]]'' (2011); ''[[Ouija: Origin of Evil]]'' (2016); and ''[[The Bye Bye Man]]'' (2017). His longest-running television role was as [[Saru (Star Trek: Discovery)|Saru]] in ''[[Star Trek: Discovery]]'' (2017–2024). He also appeared in ''[[Falling Skies]]'' (2013–2015), del Toro's ''[[The Strain (TV series)|The Strain]]'' (2014–2016), and ''[[What We Do in the Shadows (TV series)|What We Do in the Shadows]]'' (2019–2024).

==Early life and education ==
Doug Jones was born on May 24, 1960, in [[Indianapolis]], the youngest of four brothers.<ref name=officialbio>{{cite web|url=http://www.thedougjonesexperience.com/biography.htm|title=Biography|publisher=Doug Jones' official website|access-date=November 29, 2016|archive-date=October 23, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161023110729/http://thedougjonesexperience.com/biography.htm| url-status=usurped}}</ref>

He attended [[Bishop Chatard High School]]. He graduated from [[Ball State University]],<ref name=officialbio/> where he parlayed his background as a [[mime]] into portraying the school mascot "[[Charlie Cardinal]]."<ref>[http://www.thedougjonesexperience.com/ballstateinterview.htm "Charlie Cardinal Interview"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110830225656/http://www.thedougjonesexperience.com/ballstateinterview.htm|date=August 30, 2011}}. The Doug Jones Experience. Reprinted from [[Ball State University]]'s ''Alumnus Magazine''. August 2004</ref>

==Career==
Jones started his career in the television and movie industry as a 1980s [[advertising]] character, "[[Mac Tonight]]".<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Barkan |first1=Jonathan |url=http://www.dreadcentral.com/news/217879/doug-jones-mcdonalds-mac-tonight-guy|title=Doug Jones Was the McDonald's Mac Tonight Guy!|date=March 9, 2017|website=Dread Central|access-date=January 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180106063927/http://www.dreadcentral.com/news/217879/doug-jones-mcdonalds-mac-tonight-guy/|archive-date=January 6, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> He worked as a [[contortion]]ist, saying, "You'd be surprised how many times that comes into play in commercials. They'll want somebody to hold a box of [[Tide (brand)|Tide]] funny or something. I once squished into a box for a [[Television advertisement|commercial]] for relaxed fit jeans."<ref>Johnson-Ott, Edward. [http://www.nuvo.net/archive/2004/04/14/hellboys_fishguy_gets_filleted.html "Hellboy's fish-guy gets filleted."] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080820035822/http://www.nuvo.net/archive/2004/04/14/hellboys_fishguy_gets_filleted.html |date=August 20, 2008 }} Nuvo.net. April 14, 2004.</ref> In 1994, he appeared in an episode of ''[[Unsolved Mysteries]]'' as Gordon Page Jr., a young man with autism who disappeared from a treatment center in 1991.{{citation needed|date=October 2025}}

Although known mostly for his work under [[prosthetic makeup]],<ref>Bell, David Christopher (November 14, 2013). [http://www.filmschoolrejects.com/features/7-iconic-costume-actors-you-didnt-notice-in-non-costumed-roles.php "7 Iconic Costume Actors You Didn’t Notice In Non-Costumed Roles"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131114221825/http://www.filmschoolrejects.com/features/7-iconic-costume-actors-you-didnt-notice-in-non-costumed-roles.php|date=November 14, 2013}}. [[Film School Rejects]].</ref> such as the zombie William "Billy" Butcherson in the [[Walt Disney Pictures]] Halloween film ''[[Hocus Pocus (1993 film)|Hocus Pocus]]'', or the [[Morlocks#The Time Machine (2002 film)|lead spy Morlock]] in the [[The Time Machine (2002 film)|2002 remake]] of the 1960 film ''[[The Time Machine (1960 film)|The Time Machine]]'', he has also performed without prosthetics in such films as ''[[Adaptation (film)|Adaptation]]'', ''[[Mystery Men]]'', and ''[[Batman Returns]]'', and indie projects such as [[Stefan Haves]]' ''Stalled'', AntiKaiser Productions' ''Three Lives'', Phil Donlon's ''A Series of Small Things'', and as Cesare in David Fisher's [[The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari (2005 film)|2005 remake]] of the 1920 silent classic ''[[The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari]]''.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Genzlinger|first1=Neil|title=The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari – Movies – Review|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/10/25/movies/25cali.html|access-date=June 27, 2022|work=The New York Times|date=October 25, 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220514050419/https://www.nytimes.com/2006/10/25/movies/25cali.html|archive-date=May 14, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

Jones played [[Abe Sapien]] in ''[[Hellboy (2004 film)|Hellboy]]''; the voice was performed by an uncredited [[David Hyde Pierce]] in the first film, but Jones's voice was used in the sequel. Explaining the challenge of working so often in rubber suits and prosthetics, he notes, "I have to make that a part of my being and my physicality and again, acting is a full-body experience and that's a part of it when you're doing a costumed character."<ref>Topel, Fred. {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20160706115406/http://www.craveonline.com/site/157036-fantastic-four-2-doug-jones|title="Fantastic Four 2: Doug Jones: Doug Jones talks sequels, Fantastic Four and Hellboy"}}, Crave, June 15, 2007.</ref>

In 2005, he worked again with Mexican director [[Guillermo del Toro]], starring as the Faun in del Toro's multiple-[[Academy Awards|Academy Award]]-winning Spanish-language fantasy/horror project ''[[Pan's Labyrinth]]''. He also has a secondary role in the film as the Pale Man, a gruesome creature with a penchant for eating children. Working once more under heavy prosthetics in both roles, he was also required to learn large amounts of dialogue in Spanish,<ref>[http://www.canmag.com/news/4/3/6216 "Doug Jones En Espanol"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110316095803/http://www.canmag.com/news/4/3/6216 |date=March 16, 2011 }}, canmag.com; accessed March 8, 2018.</ref> although ultimately his voice was redubbed by Pablo Adan.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.behindthevoiceactors.com/movies/Pans-Labyrinth/The-Faun/|publisher=Behind the Voice Actors|title=The Faun|access-date=April 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180314181228/http://www.behindthevoiceactors.com/movies/Pans-Labyrinth/The-Faun/|archive-date=March 14, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> That same year also brought success for ''The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari'', the film receiving three awards at the Screamfest Horror Festival in Los Angeles, including the Audience Choice Award.

In 2006, Jones appeared in the feature films ''[[The Benchwarmers]]'' and ''[[Lady in the Water]]'', and reprised his role as Abe Sapien by voicing the character in the new ''[[Hellboy Animated]]'' television project, recording two 75-minute [[Animation|animated films]].{{citation needed|date=March 2019}}

In February 2007, Jones's likeness was used for [[Nvidia]]'s "Human Head" tech demo. In June 2007, he appeared in ''[[Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer]]'' as the [[Silver Surfer]], though [[Laurence Fishburne]] provided the character's voice. He reprised his role as Abe Sapien in ''[[Hellboy II: The Golden Army]]'', once more under the direction of del Toro, for which he provided both the voice and body performance. He played two other roles in the film: the Angel of Death and the Chamberlain, both under heavy prosthetics. In 2009, del Toro announced on [[BBC Radio]] that Jones would be playing the monster in his upcoming version of ''[[Frankenstein]]''.<ref>{{cite news|title=Guillermo Del Toro Casts Doug Jones in ''Frankenstein''|url=http://www.getthebigpicture.net/blog/2009/6/14/guillermo-del-toro-casts-doug-jones-in-frankenstein.html|date=June 14, 2009|access-date=June 12, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090616114714/http://www.getthebigpicture.net/blog/2009/6/14/guillermo-del-toro-casts-doug-jones-in-frankenstein.html|archive-date=June 16, 2009}}</ref>

In 2007, Jones was disappointed to learn that his voice part of the Silver Surfer had been dubbed by another actor (Fishburne) when the film was released. Upon inquiry, he determined that studio pressure had been imposed in order to add more "names" to the movie. As Jones gained greater clout in the industry, he eventually was able to add a clause to his contracts ensuring that no English dialogue of his characters would be dubbed. Roles that include other languages may be dubbed, however. This came into play in ''Pan's Labyrinth'' – Jones learned enough Spanish to voice his characters. Still, the decision was made to use a native speaker in order to access the language's nuances adequately.<ref name=IW>{{cite web|url=https://www.imaginaryworldspodcast.org/episodes/doug-jones-shapeshifter|work=Imaginary Worlds|title=Doug Jones: Shapeshifter (Episode 153)|date=December 2020|access-date=April 16, 2021}}</ref>

Jones starred as himself in ''Sockbaby 4'', the fourth installment of the Internet [[martial arts]] comedy series ''[[Sockbaby]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sockbaby.com/|title=Sockbaby|work=Sockbabt|access-date=June 13, 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080620110914/http://www.sockbaby.com/|archive-date=June 20, 2008|url-status=live}}</ref>

Jones appeared in the French-language film ''[[Gainsbourg (Vie héroïque)]]'', written and directed by French comic book author [[Joann Sfar]] and produced by Universal Europe. Jones played La Gueule ("The Mug"), the grotesque fantasy muse and malicious doppelganger who teases, guides, and accompanies [[Serge Gainsbourg]] throughout his life.<ref>{{cite book|last=Ebert|first=Roger|title=Roger Ebert's Movie Yearbook 2013: 25th Anniversary Edition|date=2012|publisher=Andrews McMeel Publishing|isbn=9781449423445|page=191|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OHTPkzKlucQC&q=%22doug+jones%22+%22La+Gueule%22&pg=PA191|language=en}}</ref> He was fitted with prosthetics designed and created by the Academy Award-winning Spanish FX shop DDT Efectos Especiales, with whom he had already worked on ''Pan's Labyrinth''; the FX technicians requested specifically that Jones be given the role of the Mug creature, due to his ability to perform (without complaining)<ref name=IW/> with heavy prosthetics and elaborate special effects. As in ''Pan's Labyrinth'', Jones performed his lines phonetically, this time speaking in French; his voice was redubbed by [[Éric Elmosnino]], who also played Gainsbourg. Director Joann Sfar liked Jones's speech patterns so much that he asked Elmosnino to mimic them when he performed the creature's lines. The film was released in France on January 20, 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.empireonline.com/movies/news/doug-jones-star-gainsbourg-biopic/|last=Hewitt|first=Chris|title=Doug Jones to star in Gainsbourg Biopic|work=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]]|date=January 20, 2009|access-date=June 27, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121015175239/http://www.empireonline.com/news/feed.asp?NID=24036|archive-date=October 15, 2012|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>[http://www.thedougjonesexperience.com/gainsbourg.htm Information on ''Gainsbourg: Vie Heroique''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100216035602/http://www.thedougjonesexperience.com/gainsbourg.htm |date=February 16, 2010}}, The Doug Jones Experience; accessed March 22, 2018.</ref><ref>[http://www.cinemotions.com/interview/90291 "Doug Jones incarne la Gueule de 'Gainsbourg'"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109142407/http://www.cinemotions.com/interview/90291|date=January 9, 2016}}, cinemotions.com; accessed March 22, 2018.</ref>

In January 2010, Jones signed a book deal with Medallion Press to model a nonfiction comedic coffee table book called ''Mime Very Own Book'', co-authored by Adam Mock and Scott Allen Perry and photographed by Eric Curtis. The book was due for publication in December 2011.<ref>[http://www.medallionpress.com/blurbs/mime.html ''Mime Very Own Book''] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100213054542/http://www.medallionpress.com/blurbs/mime.html|date=February 13, 2010}} at Medallion Press.</ref>

Jones plays Dr. Henry Vataber in the web series ''Universal Dead''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amazon.com/Universal-Dead-DB-Sweeney/dp/B00NKGD1LG/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100725233939/http://www.universaldead.com/cast.html|url-status=dead|title=Watch Universal Dead | Prime Video|archivedate=July 25, 2010|website=www.amazon.com}}</ref> In late June 2010, it was announced that ''Universal Dead'' would be made into a feature film.<ref>[http://indieintertube.tv/static/universal-dead-full-length-feature/ "Universal Dead full length feature?"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110818124246/http://indieintertube.tv/static/universal-dead-full-length-feature|date=August 18, 2011}} Indie Intertube; June 28, 2010</ref> He appeared in the independent film ''The Candy Shop'', a "modern fairy tale" shedding light upon child sex trafficking, created by the American film studio Whitestone Pictures.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.whitestonemotionpictures.com/featured/the-candy-shop-film-announcement/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718042457/http://www.whitestonemotionpictures.com/featured/the-candy-shop-film-announcement|url-status=dead|title="The Candy Shop Film Announcement"|archivedate=July 18, 2011}}</ref>

Jones played the "Operator", a fictional entity based on the Internet myth known as the "[[Slender Man]]", in ''[[Always Watching: A Marble Hornets Story]]'', a 2015 film adaptation of the popular ''[[Marble Hornets]]'' [[YouTube]] series.<ref>{{cite web|title=Web Series 'Marble Hornets' Getting Its Own Movie|url=https://my.spill.hollywood.com/profiles/blogs/web-series-marble-hornets-getting-its-own-movie?id=947994%3ABlogPost%3A6154589&page=3|archive-url=https://archive.today/20131127210203/http://my.spill.hollywood.com/profiles/blogs/web-series-marble-hornets-getting-its-own-movie?id=947994:BlogPost:6154589&page=3|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 27, 2013|publisher=Spill|access-date=December 21, 2013}}</ref>

Jones was cast as [[Saru (Star Trek: Discovery)|Saru]], a non-human [[Kelpien]] in ''[[Star Trek: Discovery]]'', which premiered on September 24, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Krishna|first1=Swapna|title=7 reasons Doug Jones is the best part of Star Trek: Discovery |url=http://www.syfy.com/syfywire/7-reasons-doug-jones-is-the-best-part-of-star-trek-discovery|website=Syfy|access-date=May 19, 2018|date=March 19, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180519121013/http://www.syfy.com/syfywire/7-reasons-doug-jones-is-the-best-part-of-star-trek-discovery|archive-date=May 19, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> That same year, Jones reunited with [[Guillermo del Toro]], this time in a romantic lead role, the Amphibian Man (the "asset") in the Academy Award-winning ''[[The Shape of Water]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.vulture.com/2017/12/how-doug-jones-became-guillermo-del-toros-favorite-monster.html|title=How Doug Jones Became Guillermo del Toro's Favorite Monster|last=Jones|first=Nate|work=Vulture|access-date=June 24, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180624093516/http://www.vulture.com/2017/12/how-doug-jones-became-guillermo-del-toros-favorite-monster.html|archive-date=June 24, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Pulver|first=Andrew|title=The Shape of Water has won the Oscar for best picture at the 90th Academy Awards|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2018/mar/05/the-shape-of-water-wins-best-picture-at-oscars-2018|website=The Guardian|access-date=March 10, 2022|date=March 5, 2018}}</ref>

In 2022, Jones reprised his role as Billy Butcherson in ''[[Hocus Pocus 2]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ew.com/movies/hocus-pocus-2-billy-butcherson-first-look-photo/|title=Billy Butcherson returns from the grave in 'Hocus Pocus 2' first look|first1=Joey Nolfi|last1=August 29|first2=2022 at 11:00 AM|last2=EDT|website=EW.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/hocus-pocus-2-doug-jones-interview-billy-butcherson-130035912.html|title='Hocus Pocus 2' star Doug Jones says when he first arrived on set, 'it was as though Elvis had risen from the dead'|website=www.yahoo.com|date=October 2022 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Jones describes himself as a "dyed-in-the-wool [[Christian]] from the Midwest", to the point that he was initially apprehensive about his role in ''Hellboy'' due to the [[Hellboy|titular character]]'s demonic nature.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.thedougjonesexperience.com/fishoutofwater~interview.htm|title=Doug Jones – Interview – Fish Out Of Water|last=Moro|first=Eric|website=The Doug Jones Experience|access-date=March 11, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160521154810/http://www.thedougjonesexperience.com/fishoutofwater~interview.htm|archive-date=May 21, 2016|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

In 1984, Jones married his college sweetheart, Laurie Pontoni. They relocated to [[Los Angeles]] in 1985 to further his acting career.<ref>

'''Ed O'Ross''' (born '''Edward Orss'''; July 5, 1949) is an American actor. His prominent roles include Itchy in ''[[Dick Tracy (1990 film)|Dick Tracy]]'', Max Kale in ''[[Walker, Texas Ranger]]'', Colonel Perry in ''[[Universal Soldier (1992 film)|Universal Soldier]]'', Lt. Touchdown in ''[[Full Metal Jacket]]'', ruthless [[Georgian people|Georgian]] mobster Viktor Rustaveli in ''[[Red Heat (1988 film)|Red Heat]]'', and police detective Cliff Willis in ''[[The Hidden (1987 film)|The Hidden]]''. He also appeared on ''[[Six Feet Under (TV series)|Six Feet Under]]'' (2001–2005), and ''[[Shark (American TV series)|Shark]]'' (2006–2008).

==Early life and education==
O'Ross was born Edward Orss on July 5, 1949 in [[Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania]].<ref name="filmr">[http://www.filmreference.com/film/28/Ed-O-Ross.html Ed O'Ross Biography (1949-)<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> He is of [[Czechoslovakia|Czechoslovak]] descent.<ref name="relishes">{{cite news |last=Owen |first=Rob |date=August 7, 2001 |title=TV Note: Munhall native relishes role on 'Six Feet Under' |url=http://old.post-gazette.com/tv/20010807tvnote0807p3.asp |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017134432/http://old.post-gazette.com/tv/20010807tvnote0807p3.asp |archive-date=October 17, 2013 |access-date=April 7, 2013 |newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]}}</ref>

O'Ross graduated from Munhall High School, where he was a star baseball player, in 1964.<ref name= MS>{{cite news| title= Life's a play, or a film, or well, a play for Munhall native Ed O'Ross| first= Maria |last= Sciullo| work= Pittsburgh Post-Gazette| url= https://www.post-gazette.com/ae/tv-radio/2018/09/18/Ed-O-Ross-actor-Pittsburgh-City-Council-Hell-s-Kitchen-award/stories/201809170103| date= September 18, 2018 | access-date= January 24, 2020}}</ref><ref name= relishes /> He subsequently attended [[Point Park College]] and [[Carnegie Tech]] (which became [[Carnegie Mellon University]]).<ref name= MS />

Prior to becoming an actor, O'Ross was a [[Boxing|boxer]], winning a [[Golden Gloves]] amateur championship in 1964.<ref name= relishes /> He was also a [[minor league baseball]] player.{{citation needed| date= January 2020}} He auditioned for two [[Major League Baseball]] teams (the [[Pittsburgh Pirates]] and [[St. Louis Cardinals]]), but was not selected.<ref name= MS />

He studied acting over several years, under [[Stella Adler]] and [[Uta Hagen]], among others.<ref name= MS />

==Career==
O'Ross has appeared in many films and series, including ''[[Red Heat (1988 film)|Red Heat]]'', ''[[Six Feet Under (TV series)|Six Feet Under]]'', and ''[[Curb Your Enthusiasm]]''. He voiced [[Agent K]] in the first season of ''[[Men in Black: The Series]]'' and was replaced by [[Gregg Berger]] in subsequent seasons. He also provided voiceover work and appeared in the music video alongside ''[[Bob Hoskins]]'' for the 1985 ''[[Paul Hardcastle]]'' song “Just For Money”.

Other films of his include ''[[Dreams of Gold: The Mel Fisher Story]]'', ''[[The Pope of Greenwich Village]]'', ''[[The Cotton Club (film)|The Cotton Club]]'', ''[[Full Metal Jacket]]'', ''[[Lethal Weapon]]'', ''[[The Hidden (1987 film)|The Hidden]]'', ''[[Action Jackson (1988 film)|Action Jackson]]'', ''[[Another 48 Hrs.]]'', ''[[Universal Soldier (1992 film)|Universal Soldier]]'', ''[[Dick Tracy (1990 film)|Dick Tracy]]'', ''[[Hoodlum (film)|Hoodlum]]'', ''[[Curious George (film)|Curious George]]'', ''[[A Green Story]],''<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 23, 2013 |title=Greek Hero in an All-American Tale |website=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/05/24/movies/a-green-story-directed-by-nika-agiashvili.html}}</ref> ''The Harsh Life of Veronica Lambert'', and ''[[Sorority Party Massacre]]''.

Guest television appearances include ''[[Stingray (1985 TV series)|Stingray]]'', ''[[Boston Legal]]'', ''[[Seinfeld]]'', ''[[Walker, Texas Ranger]]'', ''[[CSI: NY]]'', ''[[The Outsiders (American TV series)|The Outsiders]]'', and ''[[Moonlighting (TV series)|Moonlighting]]'' (in the episode "Brother, Can You Spare A Blonde?").

==Personal life==
O'Ross resides in [[New York City]] and [[Los Angeles]].<ref name= relishes />

'''Leigh Joseph McCloskey''' (born June 21, 1955) is an American artist, author, actor and self-described "visual philosopher". He is known for the immersive, hand-painted library installation '''The Hieroglyph of the Human Soul''' (sometimes abbreviated '''THOTHS'''), created in his Malibu home as an ongoing visual–philosophical environment beginning in 2001.<ref name="KCET">{{cite web |last=Watson |first=Matthew |date=December 2, 2013 |title=Leigh McCloskey: Deciphering the Hieroglyphs of the Human Soul |url=https://www.pbssocal.org/shows/artbound/leigh-mccloskey-deciphering-the-hieroglyphs-of-the-human-soul |access-date=August 22, 2025 |website=KCET / PBS SoCal – Artbound}}</ref> His pen-drawn tarot cycle was published as ''Tarot ReVisioned'' (2003), and imagery from his illuminated books ''Codex Tor'' was used on the cover and packaging of Flying Lotus’s album ''Cosmogramma'' (2010).<ref name="KCET" /> McCloskey delivered the 2024 commencement address at Pacifica Graduate Institute in Santa Barbara, California.<ref name="PacificaComm">{{cite web |date=May 24, 2024 |title=Congratulations 2024 Graduates & a Sneak Peek at Saturday's Commencement |url=https://www.pacifica.edu/pacifica-news/congratulations-2024-graduates-a-sneak-peek-at-saturdays-commencement/ |access-date=August 22, 2025 |website=Pacifica Graduate Institute}}</ref>

== Career ==

=== Visual art and THOTHS ===
[[File:LeighBYalinekras.jpg|thumb|upright|McCloskey with his collection of visual art.]]
McCloskey’s ''Hieroglyph of the Human Soul'' transforms his library into an all-over, 3D painted environment that he also uses for salons and teaching. Coverage in PBS SoCal’s ''Artbound'' details the work’s origins, alchemical motifs, and its domestic, immersive setting.<ref name="KCET" /> A 2024 profile in ''The Malibu Times'' documented a city gallery exhibition of his paintings and described his oeuvre as “phenomenally intriguing”, situating it within Malibu’s arts community.<ref name="Malibu">{{cite web |date=April 5, 2024 |title='Mining the Soul': Leigh McCloskey’s art graces Malibu City Gallery |url=https://malibutimes.com/mining-the-soul-leigh-mccloskeys-art-graces-malibu-city-gallery |access-date=August 22, 2025 |website=The Malibu Times}}</ref>

McCloskey has presented visual-philosophy talks and seminars in the United States and abroad. He spoke for the New York Open Center’s ''Esoteric Quest'' in 2006 (Central Europe program), where his session connected hermetic philosophy, tarot and image-based inquiry.<ref name="Quest06">{{cite web |date=2006 |title=An Esoteric Quest in Central Europe: From Renaissance Bohemia to Goethe’s Weimar (2006 brochure) |url=https://ralphwhite.squarespace.com/s/EsotericQuest_06Brochure.pdf |access-date=August 22, 2025 |website=New York Open Center (archival brochure)}}</ref>

In 2012, he gave a TEDxMalibu talk, “''The Painting Phoenix Arise & the Blossoming of Creation''”, using his oil painting ''Phoenix Arise'' as a demonstration of process, pattern and self-revelation through art.<ref name="TEDx">{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DlPkXeLWIZs |title=TEDxMalibu – Leigh J. McCloskey – The Blossoming of Creation |date=December 2012 |publisher=TEDx / YouTube |access-date=August 22, 2025}}</ref>

'''Robert Pine''' (born '''Granville Whitelaw Pine'''; July 10, 1941) is an American actor. He is best known as Sgt. Joseph Getraer on the television series ''[[CHiPs]]'' (1977–1983). Including ''CHiPs'', Pine has appeared in over 400 episodes of various television shows.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Keith|last=Marder|title=SMALL PARTS CAN ADD UP TO BIG CHECKS IN HOLLYWOOD|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1998-02-12-9802120250-story.html|access-date=2020-10-21|website=chicagotribune.com|date=12 February 1998 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Pine was born in [[New York City]] on July 10, 1941, the son of Virginia (née Whitelaw) and Granville Martin Pine, a patent attorney.<ref name=encyc>{{cite web |title=Robert Pine |url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/education/news-wires-white-papers-and-books/pine-robert-1941 |website=[[Encyclopedia.com]] |publisher=[[Cengage]] |access-date=December 15, 2021}}</ref><ref name=edi>{{Cite journal|title=Robert Pine|journal=TV Guide|volume=30|page=22|publisher=Triangle Publications|year=1982}}</ref> He graduated from [[Ohio Wesleyan University]] in 1963.<ref name=encyc/> He is married to [[Gwynne Gilford]], who appeared in several episodes of ''[[CHiPs]]'' as Betty Getraer, the wife of Pine's character. They have two children, actors [[Chris Pine|Chris]] and Katie.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Aggie connections move actor to help Bryan school|work=theeagle.com|url=http://www.theeagle.com/brazos_life/aggie-connections-move-actor-to-help-bryan-school/article_4cba8628-ec5d-5a7d-9e40-74d6aab42164.html|date=2010-02-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2009-06-21|title=Chris Pine: This is your captain speaking|url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/arts/la-ca-chris-pine21-2009jun21-story.html|access-date=2020-10-21|website=Los Angeles Times|language=en-US}}</ref>

Pine arrived in Hollywood in 1964, where he learned to ride horses because as a contract player with Universal Studios, he was frequently featured in westerns. Pine remained under contract with Universal until 1967.<ref>{{Cite web|title=An Enterprising Voyage with Robert Pine|url=https://www.startrek.com/news/an-enterprising-voyage-with-robert-pine|access-date=2020-10-21|website=Star Trek|language=en}}</ref> During his career he starred on the soap opera ''[[Days of Our Lives]]'' as Walter Coleman and had guest appearances in many American television shows, including ''[[Gunsmoke (TV series)|Gunsmoke]]'', ''[[Lost in Space]]'', ''[[The Silent Force (TV series)|The Silent Force]]'', ''[[The Wild Wild West]]'', ''[[Barnaby Jones]]'', ''[[Lou Grant (TV series)|Lou Grant]]'', and ''[[Knight Rider (1982 TV series)|Knight Rider]]''. On ''[[Magnum, P.I.]]'', he appeared as Thomas Magnum's father in a flashback episode. From 1977 to 1983, he starred on [[NBC]]'s ''[[CHiPs]]'' for six seasons as Sgt. Joseph Getraer, the gruff immediate supervisor to the show's two protagonists.<ref>{{Cite web|title='CHiPs' First Episode: THR's 1977 Review {{!}} Hollywood Reporter|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/review/chips-1977-review-first-episode-988325|access-date=2020-10-21|website=www.hollywoodreporter.com|date=23 March 2017 }}</ref>

In the late 1980s, Pine guest-starred as Peter Morris, [[Zack Morris (Saved by the Bell)|Zack]]'s father, in an episode of ''[[Good Morning, Miss Bliss]].'' That show went on to become ''[[Saved by the Bell]]''. In the early 1990s, Pine portrayed two villains. For ''[[California Dreams]]'', he played a wealthy racist who sabotages his daughter's friendship with drummer Tony ([[William James Jones]]).<ref>{{Cite web|title=California Dreams {{!}} TV Guide|url=https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/california-dreams/episode-7-season-1/guess-whos-coming-to-brunch/200323|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160310110839/http://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/california-dreams/episode-7-season-1/guess-whos-coming-to-brunch/200323/|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 10, 2016|access-date=2020-10-21|website=TVGuide.com|language=en}}</ref> For the [[CBS Schoolbreak Special]] ''Big Boys Don't Cry'', he played a [[pedophile]] who molests his two nephews. In 1994, he guest-starred as Bart Tupelo on CBS' ''[[Harts of the West]]'' comedy/western starring [[Beau Bridges]] and [[Lloyd Bridges]]. He reprised his role as Getraer in the 1998 [[Turner Network Television|TNT]] TV movie ''[[CHiPs '99]]''.

For ''[[Star Trek: Voyager]]'', he guest starred as the [[Akritirian]] Ambassador Liria in the Season 3 episode "[[The Chute]]". For ''[[Star Trek: Enterprise]]'', he guest-starred as [[Vulcan (Star Trek)|Vulcan]] Captain Tavin in the Season 1 episode "[[Fusion (Star Trek: Enterprise)|Fusion]]". Among his other credits are ''[[Six Feet Under (TV series)|Six Feet Under]]'', ''[[Beverly Hills 90210]]'', and ''[[Match Game]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Robert Pine - Rotten Tomatoes|url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/celebrity/robert_pine|access-date=2020-10-21|website=www.rottentomatoes.com|language=en}}</ref> In September 2013, he appeared as Grandpa Jack in [[Kaiser Permanente]]'s television ad "Thrive - Perfectly Ordinary". He was the voice of the Bishop of Arendelle in Disney's 2013 animated movie ''[[Frozen (2013 film)|Frozen]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Frozen (2013)|url=http://www.bfi.org.uk/films-tv-people/524365c72096c|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307152928/http://www.bfi.org.uk/films-tv-people/524365c72096c|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 7, 2016|website=BFI Film Forever|publisher=British Film Institute|access-date=27 March 2018}}</ref>

'''Michael Pataki''' (January 16, 1938 – April 15, 2010) was an American actor of stage, film and television.<ref>Obituary ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'', May 5, 2010; p. AA7.</ref>

==Early life==
Pataki was born in [[Youngstown, Ohio]], to Hungarian parents, the youngest of three children. He had an elder brother and an elder sister. He attended the [[University of Southern California]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Variety |date=2010-04-20 |title=Character actor Pataki dies of cancer |url=https://variety.com/2010/scene/people-news/character-actor-pataki-dies-of-cancer-1118018051/ |access-date=2025-08-24 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> with a double major in [[political science]] and [[drama]]. His career was launched at a [[summer stock]] festival in [[Edinburgh]] in 1966 as Jerry in ''[[The Zoo Story]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Michael Pataki Autographs, Memorabilia & Collectibles {{!}} HistoryForSale |url=https://www.historyforsale.com/signer-memorabilia/michael-pataki/231336 |access-date=2025-12-28 |website=HistoryForSale - Autographs, Collectibles & Memorabilia |language=en}}</ref>

==Television career==
Pataki had a co-starring role on the 1974–75 groundbreaking ABC-TV series ''[[Get Christie Love!]]'' playing Officer Pete Gallagher, Christie Love's bumbling but well-meaning sidekick with the dream to one day be a technical advisor on a TV cop show. Despite being the first detective TV series with an [[African Americans|African American]] female lead, the characters of Christie and Pete rarely discussed race. 

Pataki appeared as a guest star in numerous television productions, from the black-and-white days of ''[[Hawaiian Eye]]'', ''[[M Squad]]'', ''[[The Twilight Zone (1959 TV series)|The Twilight Zone]]'', ''[[Ripcord (TV series)|Ripcord]]'', ''[[Combat! (TV series)|Combat!]]'', and ''[[My Favorite Martian]]'', to early [[Color television|color]] shows such as ''[[The Flying Nun]]'', ''[[All in the Family]]'', ''[[Mr. Terrific (TV series)|Mr. Terrific]]'', ''[[Garrison's Gorillas]]'', ''[[Bonanza]]'', ''[[Run for Your Life (TV series)|Run for Your Life]]'', ''[[Mission: Impossible (1966 TV series)|Mission: Impossible]]'', ''[[Mannix]]'', ''[[Batman (TV series)|Batman]]'', and ''[[Felony Squad]]''. He was also a regular on ''[[Friends and Lovers (TV series)|Paul Sand in Friends and Lovers]]'', and ''[[The Amazing Spider-Man (TV series)|The Amazing Spider-Man]]'', and had a re-occurring role on ''[[McCloud (TV series)|McCloud]]'' as well. One of his most famous roles was as Korax, the brash, loudmouthed [[Klingon]] who provoked the bar fight in "[[The Trouble with Tribbles]]" episode of ''[[Star Trek: The Original Series|Star Trek]]''.<ref name="Ulster">{{cite web |date=March 11, 2021 |author=LAURIE ULSTER |title=13 Original Series Actors Who Couldn't Get Enough Trek |url=https://www.startrek.com/news/13-tos-actors-who-appeared-on-other-tv-treks-decades-later |website=StarTrek.com }}</ref>.  He also played Governor Karnas in the ''[[Star Trek: The Next Generation]]'' episode "[[Too Short a Season]]"<ref name="Ulster" /> making Pataki one of the few ''Star Trek'' actors that appeared in both the original series and ''[[Star Trek: The Next Generation|The Next Generation]]''.  

Pataki played [[George Liquor]] in the episodes of ''[[The Ren & Stimpy Show]]'' titled "[[Dog Show (The Ren & Stimpy Show)|Dog Show]]" and "[[Man's Best Friend (The Ren & Stimpy Show)|Man's Best Friend]]"; he would also play various characters after series creator [[John Kricfalusi]] was terminated from the series, while continuing to play the latter role in subsequent Kricfalusi projects until Pataki's death, with his last appearance being in the posthumously released 2019 short ''Cans Without Labels''.  He was also the voice of The Cow in ''[[Mighty Mouse: The New Adventures]]'', along with many other secondary characters. Pataki played a guest spot on ''[[Happy Days]]'' Season 4 as Myron "Count" Malachi, one half of the Malachi brothers. His role was notable for his line "Let the pigeons loose." He played a Russian defector in the episode "The Americanization of Ivan" in ''[[WKRP in Cincinnati]]''.

==Film career==
Pataki's film credits included ''[[Airport '77]]'' (1977), ''[[Spider-Man (1977 film)|Spider-Man]]'' (1977), ''[[Love at First Bite]]'' (1979), ''[[The Onion Field (film)|The Onion Field]]'' (1979), ''[[Raise the Titanic (film)|Raise the Titanic]]'' (1980), ''[[Remo Williams: The Adventure Begins]]'' (1985), and many others. He also appeared in ''[[Rocky IV]]'' (1985), as Nicoli Koloff, the sports administrator for [[Ivan Drago]] and had a memorable moment in [[Ron Howard]]'s [[Sexual comedy|sex comedy]] ''[[Night Shift (1982 film)|Night Shift]]'' as a man who moons an entire courtroom.

Pataki has also had his fair share of [[B movie]] roles in titles such as ''[[The Last Porno Flick]]'' (1974), ''[[Carnal Madness]]'' a.k.a. ''Delinquent Schoolgirls'' (1975) with [[George Buck Flower]], [[Colleen Brennan]], and others. In ''[[Dracula's Dog]]'' (1977), he played opposite [[Reggie Nalder]] and [[José Ferrer]] as a descendant of [[Count Dracula|Dracula]] who is being [[Stalking|stalked]] by a [[Vampire|vampiric]] [[Dobermann|Doberman Pinscher]]. His other horror titles included ''[[Grave of the Vampire]]'' (1972), ''[[The Baby (film)|The Baby]]'' (1973), ''[[Dead & Buried]]'' (1981) and ''[[Halloween 4: The Return of Michael Myers]]'' (1988). He also directed [[Richard Basehart]] in ''[[Mansion of the Doomed]]'' (1976).

=== Other film work ===
Pataki directed the 1977 [[Softcore pornography|soft-core]] [[Bedroom farce|sex farce]] ''[[Cinderella (1977 film)|Cinderella]]''. He also produced a 1981 TV presentation of ''[[Pippin (musical)|Pippin]]'' with [[David Sheehan]], starring [[William Katt]].<ref name=":0"/>

==Death==
Pataki died from cancer on April 15, 2010, at the age of 72.<ref name=":0"/> He completed his recording for George Liquor for ''Cans Without Labels'' before his death<ref name="kickstarter">{{Cite web |url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/1056985656/john-ks-cans-without-labels |title=John K's "Cans Without Labels" }}</ref> and the short was dedicated to his memory.

Career == [[File:Mod Squad 1971.JPG|thumb|The ''Mod Squad'' main cast in 1971 from left: Williams, [[Peggy Lipton]] and [[Michael Cole (actor)|Michael Cole]]]]Williams first appeared on [[Broadway (theatre)|Broadway]] in ''The Long Dream'' (1960). Continuing his work on stage, he appeared in ''Walk in Darkness'' (1963), ''Sarah and the Sax'' (1964), ''Doubletalk'' (1964), and ''[[King John (play)|King John]]''.{{cite news| url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/marcberman1/2021/06/06/the-mod-squad-star-clarence-williams-iii-dies-at-81/| title='The Mod Squad Star' Clarence Williams III Dies At 81| magazine=[[Forbes]]| date=June 6, 2021| first=Marc| last=Berman| access-date=June 7, 2021}} His breakout theatrical role was in [[William Hanley]]'s ''Slow Dance on the Killing Ground'', for which he received a [[Tony Award]] nomination. The ''[[New York Times]]'' drama critic [[Howard Taubman]] wrote of his performance, "Mr. Williams glides like a dancer, giving his long, fraudulently airy speeches the inner rhythms of fear and showing the nakedness of terror when he ceases to pretend." He also served as artist-in-residence at [[Brandeis University]] in 1966.{{cite news| url=http://timesmachine.nytimes.com/timesmachine/1964/12/01/118691271.html?action=click&contentCollection=Archives&module=LedeAsset®ion=ArchiveBody&pgtype=article&pageNumber=50/%3E| title=The Theater: 'Slow Dance on the Killing Ground'; William Hanley Makes His Broadway Debut Story of Tortured Trio Opens at Plymouth| newspaper=[[The New York Times]]| date=December 1, 1964| access-date=January 13, 2019| url-access=subscription}} Williams' breakout television role was as undercover cop Linc Hayes on the popular [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] [[counterculture of the 1960s|counterculture]] police television series ''[[The Mod Squad]]'' (1968), along with fellow relative unknowns [[Michael Cole (actor)|Michael Cole]] and [[Peggy Lipton]]. After the series ended in 1973, he worked in a variety of genres on stage and screen, from comedy (''[[I'm Gonna Git You Sucka]]'', ''[[Half-Baked]]'') to sci-fi (''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]''), and drama (''[[Purple Rain (film)|Purple Rain]]''). Spanning over forty years, his career included the role of [[Prince (musician)|Prince]]'s tormented father, who was also a musician, in ''[[Purple Rain (film)|Purple Rain]]'' (1984), A guest appearance in ''[[Miami Vice]]'' (1985), a recurring role in the surreal TV series ''[[Twin Peaks]]'' (1990), a good cop in ''[[Deep Cover (1992 film)|Deep Cover]]'' (1992), a rioter in the mini-series ''Against the Wall'' (1994), and [[Wesley Snipes]]' chemically dependent father in ''Sugar Hill'' (1993). His other roles on television include ''[[Hill Street Blues]]'', the Canadian cult classic ''[[The Littlest Hobo]]'', ''[[Miami Vice]]'', ''[[The Highwayman (TV series)|The Highwayman]]'', ''[[Burn Notice]]'', ''[[Everybody Hates Chris]]'', ''[[Justified (TV series)|Justified]]'', ''[[Cold Case]]'', and ''[[Law & Order]]''. He can be seen in films such as ''[[52 Pick-Up]]'', ''[[Life (1999 film)|Life]]'', ''[[The Cool World]]'', ''[[Deep Cover (1992 film)|Deep Cover]]'', ''[[Tales from the Hood]]'', ''[[Half-Baked]]'', ''[[King: A Filmed Record... Montgomery to Memphis]]'', ''[[Hoodlum (film)|Hoodlum]]'', ''[[Frogs for Snakes]]'', ''[[Starstruck (1998 film)|Starstruck]]'', ''[[The General's Daughter (film)|The General's Daughter]]'', ''[[Reindeer Games]]'', ''[[Impostor (2002 film)|Impostor]]'', and as the early jazz musician [[Jelly Roll Morton]] in ''[[The Legend of 1900]]''. He also played a supporting role as [[George Wallace]]'s fictional African-American butler and caretaker in the 1997 [[TNT (U.S. TV network)|TNT]] film ''[[George Wallace (film)|George Wallace]]''. From 2003 to 2007, Williams had a recurring role as Philby Cross in the ''[[Mystery Woman]]'' film series on the [[Hallmark Channel]]. He appeared in all but the first of the eleven films alongside [[Kellie Martin]] ([[J.E. Freeman]] played Philby in the Mystery Woman first film). In the seventh (''[[Mystery Woman#Movies|Mystery Woman: At First Sight]]'') film, he reunited with his ''Mod Squad'' co-star Michael Cole. He played [[Bumpy Johnson]] in the film ''[[American Gangster (film)|American Gangster]]''.{{cite news| url=https://www.cnn.com/2007/SHOWBIZ/Movies/11/01/review.gangster/index.html| title=Review: Brilliant Washington powers 'Gangster'| work=[[CNN]]| date=November 1, 2007}} From 2005 to 2007, Williams had another recurring role as the voice of Councilor Andam on the Disney animated series ''[[American Dragon: Jake Long]]''. ==Personal life== [[File:Gloria Foster and Clarence Williams Mod Squad 1970.JPG|thumb|Foster and Williams in ''The Mod Squad'' episode in 1970. Foster guest-starred as a blind friend of Linc Hayes.]] Williams married the actress [[Gloria Foster]] in 1967.{{cite news| url=https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-57382649| title=Clarence Williams III: Tributes paid to late star of Purple Rain and The Mod Squad| date=June 7, 2021| work=[[BBC News]]| access-date=March 25, 2023}} They worked together on ''[[The Mod Squad]]''; Foster made two guest appearances.{{cite news| url=https://movieweb.com/clarence-williams-iii-dead/| title=Clarence Williams III Dies, Mod Squad and Tales from the Hood Star Was 81| last=Lund| first=Anthony| website=[[MovieWeb]]| date=June 8, 2021| access-date=March 25, 2023}} The two also acted in a 1964 film ''[[The Cool World]]''. In 1984, they filed for divorce, but remained friends. They had no children. Williams announced Foster's death in 2001. His oft-collaborator, director [[John Frankenheimer]], considered Williams one of the greatest [[character actors]] of his lifetime, saying “Clarence’ll put the fear of God in you.” ===Death=== Williams died in [[Los Angeles]], on June 4, 2021, at the age of 81, from [[colon cancer]].{{cite news |last=Haring |first=Bruce |date=June 6, 2021 |title=Clarence Williams III Dies: 'Linc' On 'The Mod Squad' Was 81 |url=https://deadline.com/2021/06/clarence-williams-iii-dead-linc-the-mod-squad-obituary-81-1234770213/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210606204535/https://deadline.com/2021/06/clarence-williams-iii-dead-linc-the-mod-squad-obituary-81-1234770213/ |archive-date=June 6, 2021 |access-date=June 6, 2021 |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}{{cite news |last=Barnes |first=Mike |date=June 6, 2021 |title=Clarence Williams III, Linc on 'The Mod Squad,' Dies at 81 |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/clarence-williams-iii-mod-squad-dies-at-81-1234963703/ |access-date=June 7, 2021 |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}} He is buried in [[St. Charles / Resurrection Cemeteries|St Charles Cemetery]] in [[East Farmingdale, New York]]. == Selected filmography == === Film === {| class="wikitable sortable" |- ! '''Michael Bell''' (born July 30, 1938) is an American actor who is most active in voice over roles. He has acted in video games and animated series, including ''[[Legacy of Kain]]'', ''[[The Transformers (TV series)|The Transformers]]'', ''[[G.I. Joe: A Real American Hero (1983 TV series)|G.I. Joe: A Real American Hero]]'', ''[[The Houndcats]]'', ''[[Rugrats]]'', ''[[The Smurfs (1981 TV series)|The Smurfs]]'', ''[[The Incredible Hulk (1982 TV series)|The Incredible Hulk]]'' and ''[[Snorks]]'' and appeared on-screen in film and television, including the TV programs ''[[Dallas (TV series)|Dallas]]'' and ''[[Star Trek]]''.

==Early life==
Michael Bell was born on July 30, 1938,<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael Bell |url=https://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/person/13107%7C111293/Michael-Bell |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140204144122/http://www.tcm.com/tcmdb/person/13107%7C111293/Michael-Bell/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 4, 2014 |website=[[Turner Classic Movies]] |access-date=April 16, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Arnold |first1=Mark |title=Think Pink: The Story of DePatie-Freleng |date=2015 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PJmeDwAAQBAJ}} "Voice actor Michael Bell (1938-)"</ref> in [[Brooklyn]], New York, to a Jewish family.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.villagevoice.com/2013/08/29/ten-fascinating-facts-from-slimed-the-new-oral-history-of-90s-nickelodeon/| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170922145352/https://www.villagevoice.com/2013/08/29/ten-fascinating-facts-from-slimed-the-new-oral-history-of-90s-nickelodeon/| url-status=dead| archive-date=September 22, 2017| title=Ten Fascinating Facts from Slimed!, the new Oral History of '90s Nickelodeon| first=Inkoo| last=Kang| date=August 22, 2013| work=[[The Village Voice]]| access-date=September 22, 2017}}</ref>

==Career==
===Live-action roles===
His live action film career has included roles in films such as ''[[Thunder Alley (1967 film)|Thunder Alley]]'' (1967), ''[[Blue (1968 film)|Blue]]'' (1968), ''[[The Proud Rider]]'' (1971)<ref>[https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067624/?ref_=nm_flmg_act_157 "The Proud Rider] at [[IMDb]].com (retrieved January 7, 2018); [https://letterboxd.com/film/the-proud-rider/ "The Proud Rider] at Letterboxd.com (retrieved January 7, 2018)</ref> ''[[Brother John (film)|Brother John]]'' (1971), ''[[Rollercoaster (1977 film)|Rollercoaster]]'' (1977), ''[[Fast Company (1979 film)|Fast Company]]'' (1979), ''[[How to Beat the High Cost of Living]]'' (1980) and ''[[C.H.U.D. II: Bud the C.H.U.D.]]'' (1989). Bell also appeared in live-action exploitation shorts and [[Public Service Announcement|PSAs]] - scare films made in California during the early 1960s, ranging in content from venereal disease (''Damaged Goods'') to psychedelic drug abuse (''Trip To Where'').

He appeared in the ''[[Star Trek: The Next Generation]]'' pilot episode, "[[Encounter at Farpoint]]", as Bandi administrator Groppler Zorn, and in the ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'' episodes "[[The Homecoming (Star Trek: Deep Space Nine)|The Homecoming]]" as a [[Bajoran]] and in "[[The Maquis]]."

Bell appeared in multiple episodes of ''[[Dallas (TV series)|Dallas]]'' as Les Crowley during the 1980–81 season, in ''[[M*A*S*H (TV series)|M*A*S*H]]'' in the episode "Souvenirs" as Willie Stratton and also guest starred in two episodes of ''[[Three's Company]]'' as Rama Mageesh and Michael, a sleazy dance instructor in the sixth-season episode "Some of That Jazz" (1981). Bell played Bill Duncan, Sabrina ([[Kate Jackson]])'s ex-husband on ''[[Charlie's Angels]]'', as well as appearing as King Edward Spencer on Jackson's series ''[[Scarecrow and Mrs. King]]''. In 1970, he appeared in an episode of ''[[The Silent Force (TV series)|The Silent Force]]''.

===1970s and 1980s voice work===
Bell had an important part in animated entertainment in the 1970s and 1980s. His first voice role was that of Stutz, the leader of ''[[The Houndcats]]''. In 1973, he was Mark on the [[Hanna-Barbera]] series ''[[Speed Buggy]]''. He voiced Redbeard the Pirate's Ghost in ''[[The New Scooby-Doo Movies]]'' episode "The Ghostly Creep from the Deep" as the second Redbeard themed monster in Scooby-Doo. Bell also reprised Mark on the same cartoon in the episode "Weird Winds of Winona".

From 1977 to 1984, Michael Bell played two of his best-known roles, [[The Wonder Twins|Zan]] and [[Gleek (Super Friends)|Gleek]] on various ''[[Super Friends]]'' incarnations. He also voiced [[The Riddler]] on ''[[Challenge of the Superfriends]]''. He also provided the voice of [[Lex Luthor]] as a young man, in the episode "History of Doom". However, [[G. Stanley Jones|Stan Jones]] was the voice of the adult Luthor throughout the series. Bell later played Luthor in the 1988 ''[[Superman (TV series)|Superman]]'' series.

He was also Doctor Ben Cooper in ''[[Jana of the Jungle]]'' and in 1979, he voiced the title character of ''[[The Plastic Man Comedy/Adventure Show]]'' and later made a guest appearance as [[Doctor Octopus]] in another superhero show, ''[[Spider-Man and His Amazing Friends]]''.

Outside of animation, Bell performed on records and commercials, including the Young Man in [[A&M Records]]' ''Story of Halloween Horror'' album in 1977, and Parkay Margarine and Mug Root Beer ads. Bell provided the overdubbing of [[Peter Criss]]' dialogue in the band [[Kiss (band)|KISS's]] TV movie ''[[KISS Meets the Phantom of the Park]]''. In 1980, he provided the voice of the title character in ''The B.B. Beegle Show'', an unsold TV show pilot that featured puppets.

Throughout the 1980s, Michael Bell starred in four hit animated series;
* as [[Grouchy Smurf]], Lazy Smurf, [[Handy Smurf]] and Johan in ''[[The Smurfs (1981 TV series)|The Smurfs]]''
* as [[Prowl (Transformers)|Prowl]], [[Scrapper (Transformers)|Scrapper]], [[Sideswipe (Transformers)|Sideswipe]], Bombshell, [[First Aid (Transformers)|First Aid]], Swoop, Gort, [[Brainstorm (Transformers)|Brainstorm]] and Doctor Fujiyama in ''[[The Transformers (TV series)|The Transformers]]'' and ''[[The Transformers: The Movie]]''
* as [[Duke (G.I. Joe)|Duke]], Xamot, [[Blowtorch (G.I. Joe)|Blowtorch]] and numerous others in ''[[G.I. Joe: A Real American Hero (1985 TV series)|G.I. Joe: A Real American Hero]]'' and ''[[G.I. Joe: The Movie]]''
* as Lance & Sven in ''[[Voltron]]: Defender of the Universe''.

He also starred in the 1982 animated series ''[[The Incredible Hulk (1982 TV series)|The Incredible Hulk]]''. [[Hulk|The Hulk]] was voiced by [[Bob Holt (actor)|Bob Holt]], while his human side, Bruce Banner, was played by Bell. In a 2004 interview, Bell joked about how Holt would be annoyed that he was growling his throat out, while Bell's acting was much easier on his throat.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://hulk.toonzone.net/Credits/voices/Bell/InterviewMB.html| publisher=The Incredible Hulk 1982 Cartoon Webpage| title=An Interview with Michael Bell| date=November 2004}}</ref>

During this time, the actor also played Hiro Taka on ''[[Spiral Zone]]'' and Allstar Seaworthy on ''[[The Snorks]]'' (1984-1989)

===Later voice work===
[[File:Michael Bell 2015.jpg|thumb|Bell at the 2015 Retro Con]]
Bell continues to work in animation in the 1990s and into the 21st century in movies and television, with roles such as [[Quackerjack]] from [[Disney]]'s ''[[Darkwing Duck]]'', Aziz on ''[[Aladdin (animated TV series)|Aladdin]]'' and [[Ezekiel Rage]] on ''[[The Real Adventures of Jonny Quest]]''. He was also featured as Opus in the Bloom County television special ''A Wish for Wings That Work''.

From 1991 to 2004, in the ''[[Rugrats]]'' and ''[[All Grown Up!]]'', he voiced three of the main characters' parents; [[Drew Pickles]], Charles Finster Sr., and Boris Kropotkin.

Bell did the voices of Drake on ''[[W.I.T.C.H. (TV series)|W.I.T.C.H.]]'', Max Hauser, Duke's Dad on ''[[G.I. Joe: Renegades]]'', Willy Wachowski on ''[[Handy Manny]]'' and additional roles in ''[[Tangled]]'' (2010).

In 2018, Bell reprised his role as Quackerjack on the reboot of ''[[DuckTales (2017 TV series)|DuckTales]]''.

===Video game voice work===
He is also a prolific voice in video games, which include ''[[Soldier of Fortune II: Double Helix]]'', ''[[Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos]]'', ''[[Diablo II: Lord of Destruction]]'', ''[[Age of Empires III]],'' ''[[Baldur's Gate]],'' ''[[Ratchet & Clank]]'', the character Dark Fact in the game ''[[Ys I & II]]'', and the character [[Raziel (Legacy of Kain)|Raziel]] in four games in the ''[[Legacy of Kain]]'' series, among many others. He also plays the Fear in [[Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater]].

===Documentary narration===
He narrated the documentary programs ''[[Earth's Fury]]'' (also known as ''Anatomy of Disaster'' internationally), ''Expeditions to the Edge'', ''Bullet Catchers'' and ''Mysteries of Asia'', while he narrated some episodes of ''[[E! True Hollywood Story]]''.

===Stage roles===
In 1983, he and his future wife Victoria Carroll opened The West End Playhouse in Van Nuys. The two of them organized, wrote, directed, and acted in dozens of productions.

One of the most notable was ''The Ladies of the Camillias'' in which Bell played the villain Ivan and Victoria starred as Madame Sarah Bernhardt. The play won multiple Drama Logue Awards.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/280581845| title=Stage Review ''Ladies of the Camellias'' Matches Duse, Bernhardt at West End| last=Koehler| first=Robert| date=September 16, 1988| work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

He served as the theater's director until 1988, when by mutual agreement to devote more time to their child, Bell and Carroll sold the theater to Edmund Gaynes and Pamela Hall.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=LA&p_theme=la&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EF51B40EEA51DB7&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM| title=Stage News & Notes| date=December 9, 1988| work=[[The Daily News of Los Angeles]]}}</ref>

===Voice director===
Bell was the voice director for ''[[Kidd Video]]'', ''[[Fox's Peter Pan & the Pirates|Peter Pan and the Pirates]]'', as well as the web series ''[[LeBrons|The LeBrons]]''.

==Union activism==
On March 30, 2012, the [[Screen Actors Guild]] (SAG) and the [[American Federation of Television and Radio Artists]] (AFTRA) completed a merger of equals forming a new union [[SAG-AFTRA]]. As a result of this merger, a group of actors including Bell, fellow voice actors [[Wendy Schaal]], [[Clancy Brown]], Schaal's former stepmother [[Valerie Harper]], and other actors including former SAG President [[Edward Asner]], [[Martin Sheen]], [[Ed Harris]], and [[Nancy Sinatra]] immediately sued against the current SAG President [[Ken Howard]] and several SAG Vice Presidents to overturn the merger and separate the (now merged) two unions because of their claims that the election was improper.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr-esq/sag-aftra-anti-merger-lawsuit-drops-demand-295573| work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]| title=SAG/AFTRA Anti Merger Lawsuit Drops Demands| first= Jonathan| last=Handel| date=February 27, 2012}}</ref> The plaintiffs dropped their lawsuit several months later.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/envelope/la-xpm-2012-may-16-la-et-ct-sag-merger-20120516-story.html| website=The New York Times| last=Verrier| first=Richard| title=SAG-AFTRA merger opponents to drop lawsuit}}</ref>

==Inventor==
In 1991, Bell and his colleague [[Melanie Chartoff]] conceived the Grayway Rotating Drain, a [[graywater]] recycling device for reuse of shower and sink water in the home. The following year, they finished and patented the product with the help of Ronald K. Ford.<ref>*{{US patent|5274861}}, "Gray water recycling system" (January 4, 1994)
</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.graywayrotatingdrain.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180805144936/http://www.graywayrotatingdrain.com/  |archive-date=August 5, 2018 |title=GRAYWAY ROTATING DRAIN - Graywater Recycling Device |website=graywayrotatingdrain.com |via=archive.org |access-date=September 23, 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://members.aol.com:80/graywaydrain2003/questions.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031118183540/http://members.aol.com/graywaydrain2003/questions.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 18, 2003|title=Grayway FAQ|website=members.aol.com:80/graywaydrain2003|access-date=September 23, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=IO1HAAAAIBAJ&pg=5228,4455295&dq=melanie+chartoff&hl=en|title=Melanie Chartoff is also an inventor|newspaper=[[Record-Journal]]|date=September 28, 1992|access-date=July 2, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect1=PTO2&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=/netahtml/PTO/search-bool.html&r=1&f=G&l=50&co1=&d=PTXT&s1=5,274,861.PN.|title=United States Patent: 5274861 - Gray water recycling system|website=uspto.gov|access-date=September 23, 2018}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Bell has been married to actress [[Victoria Carroll]] since 1984.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CCUSa_GmDo8C&q=Victoria+Carroll&pg=PA29| title=Glamour Girls of Sixties Hollywood: Seventy-Five Profiles| first=Tom| last=Lisanti| publisher=McFarland| date=September 25, 2007 | isbn=9780786431724|access-date=September 22, 2017}}</ref> Together they have a daughter, [[Ashley Bell (actress)|Ashley Bell]], who is also an actress.<ref>{{cite web| url= https://movies.nytimes.com/person/1358396/Ashley-Bell | archive-url= https://archive.today/20130619215805/http://movies.nytimes.com/person/1358396/Ashley-Bell | url-status= dead | archive-date= June 19, 2013 | department= Movies & TV Dept. | work= [[The New York Times]] | title= Ashley Bell | access-date= August 28, 2013}}</ref> He is an [[animal rights]] activist. He is the godfather of actor [[Steve Guttenberg]], who cites Bell as his inspiration to become an actor.

Bell served on the board of directors of the Los Angeles Local of [[SAG-AFTRA]] in 2016 until 2019.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.sagaftra.org/locals/los-angeles/about-our-local/local-board| title=Local Board| publisher=SAG-AFTRA}}</ref>

'''Paul Francis Tompkins''' (born September 12, 1968)<ref name=NYT3>{{cite news |title=A Pop-Culture Show Looks for Attitude With Heart |first=Melena |last=Ryzik |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/10/15/arts/television/15best.html |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=October 14, 2008 |access-date=May 31, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=James Bonding #001: Dr. No with Paul F. Tompkins |url=https://archive.nerdist.com/james-bonding-001-dr-no-with-paul-f-tompkins/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029201042/http://www.nerdist.com/2013/09/james-bonding-001-dr-no-with-paul-f-tompkins/ |archive-date=October 29, 2013 |access-date=October 26, 2013 |publisher=Nerdist.com}}</ref><ref name="REVERB2" /> is an American comedian, actor, and writer. He has worked in television on such programs as ''[[BoJack Horseman]]'', ''[[Mr. Show with Bob and David]]'', ''[[Real Time with Bill Maher]]'', and ''[[Best Week Ever]]'',<ref name=REVERB2/><ref name=AUSTINCH>{{cite news |title=Battleship Paul F. Tompkins |first=Steve |last=Birmingham |url=http://www.austinchronicle.com/arts/2005-04-22/267599/ |newspaper=Austin Chronicle |date=April 22, 2005 |access-date=May 31, 2012}}</ref><ref name=SFBAYGUARD>{{cite news |first=George |last=Chen |date=January 16, 2008 |title=Getting Impersonal with Paul F. Tompkins |url=http://www.sfbg.com/pixel_vision/2008/01/16/getting-impersonal-paul-f-tompkins |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121017044550/http://www.sfbg.com/pixel_vision/2008/01/16/getting-impersonal-paul-f-tompkins |archive-date=October 17, 2012 |newspaper=[[San Francisco Bay Guardian]] |access-date=May 31, 2012}}</ref> later renamed ''Best Week Ever with Paul F. Tompkins''.<ref name=NYT3/><ref name=AVCLUB1>{{cite web |last=Heisler |first=Steve |author2=Wolinsky, David |date=March 12, 2009 |title=Who the Hell Is Paul F. Tompkins? |url=http://www.avclub.com/chicago/articles/who-the-hell-is-paul-f-tompkins,24941/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100510080146/http://www.avclub.com/chicago/articles/who-the-hell-is-paul-f-tompkins,24941/ |archive-date=May 10, 2010 |department=11 Questions (column) |work=[[The A.V. Club]] |publisher=[[The Onion]] |access-date=May 31, 2012}}</ref>

He has numerous appearances on podcasts, including his 200-plus appearances on ''[[Comedy Bang! Bang!]]'' He has been the host of the [[Fusion Channel]] talk show ''[[No, You Shut Up!]]'', ''[[The Dead Authors Podcast]]'', the online Made Man interview series ''Speakeasy with Paul F. Tompkins'', the [[Earwolf]] podcast ''[[Spontaneanation|Spontaneanation with Paul F. Tompkins]]'', and ''The Pod F. Tompkast'', which was ranked #1 by ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' on their list of "The 10 Best Comedy Podcasts of the Moment" in 2011.<ref name=ROLLINGSTONE>{{cite news |title=The 10 Best Comedy Podcasts of the Moment |first=Berkowitz |last=Joe |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/news/the-10-best-comedy-podcasts-of-the-moment-20110406 |newspaper=Rolling Stone |date=April 6, 2011 |access-date=May 31, 2012 |archive-date=October 30, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111030064104/http://www.rollingstone.com/culture/news/the-10-best-comedy-podcasts-of-the-moment-20110406 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He is a main cast member of the ''[[Superego (podcast)|Superego]]'' podcast and was a regular player on ''[[Thrilling Adventure Hour]]'' podcast, which ended in 2015. He is hosting the podcasts ''Threedom'' and ''The Neighborhood Listen'' as well as the independent podcast ''Stay F. Homekins''.

Tompkins voiced [[Mr. Peanutbutter]], an anthropomorphic yellow {{not a typo|labrador}}, on the [[Netflix]] animated series ''[[BoJack Horseman]]'' from 2014 to 2020. He has appeared in drama films like ''[[There Will Be Blood]]'' and ''[[The Informant!]]''. In 2021, he had a recurring role on the sitcom ''[[Rutherford Falls]]''.

In December 2014, ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]'' named his [[Twitter]] one of "The 75 Best Twitter Accounts of 2014", ranking it at #70.<ref name="The 75 Best Twitter Accounts of 2014 :: Comedy :: Lists :: Paste">{{cite news |last1=Hongo |first1=Hudson |date=December 15, 2014 |title=The 75 Best Twitter Accounts of 2014 |work=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]] |url=http://www.pastemagazine.com/blogs/lists/2014/12/the-75-best-twitter-accounts-of-2014.html |access-date=December 28, 2014 |archive-date=September 7, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170907170005/https://www.pastemagazine.com/blogs/lists/2014/12/the-75-best-twitter-accounts-of-2014.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Tompkins was born on September 12, 1968, in [[Philadelphia]]. He is the fifth of six children.<ref name=REVERB2/><ref name=TORSTAR>{{cite news |title=300 tweets summon a joker to Toronto |first=Garnet |last=Fraser |url=https://www.thestar.com/entertainment/whatson/article/715425--300-tweets-summon-a-joker-to-toronto |newspaper=[[Toronto Star]] |date=October 25, 2009 |access-date=May 31, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121019015835/http://www.thestar.com/entertainment/whatson/article/715425--300-tweets-summon-a-joker-to-toronto |archive-date=October 19, 2012 }}</ref><ref name=AVCLUB2>{{cite web |title=Interview – Paul F. Tompkins |last=Ryan |first=Kyle |date=July 19, 2007 |url=https://www.avclub.com/paul-f-tompkins-1798211854 |work=[[The A.V. Club]] |publisher=[[The Onion]] |access-date=May 31, 2012}}</ref> He attended [[Bishop McDevitt High School (Wyncote, Pennsylvania)|Bishop McDevitt High School]] in [[Wyncote, Pennsylvania]].

==Career==
===Early work===
In 1986, Tompkins first performed comedy at 17 years of age at The Comedy Works in Philadelphia (a club now located in [[Bristol, Pennsylvania]]), where he performed as half of a [[sketch comedy]] duo with [[Rick Roman]].<ref name=AVCLUB2/><ref>{{Cite web |title=Monthly Schedule |url=http://www.comedyworksbristol.com/ |publisher=The Comedy Works |access-date=June 18, 2016}}</ref><ref name=IMPOSE>{{cite web |url=http://www.imposemagazine.com/features/an-interview-with-paul-f-tompki |title=Paul F. Tompkins |last=Downs |first=Gordon |date=July 26, 2007 |work=Impose Magazine |publisher=Impose |access-date=May 31, 2012}}</ref><ref name=CITYPAPER>{{cite news |first=Patrick |last=Rapa |date=August 17, 2010 |title=Stay Classy, Philadelphia: An Open Mic with Paul F. Tompkins, the Nicest Guy in Comedy |url=https://issuu.com/phillycp/docs/cp_2010-08-19/1 |newspaper=[[Philadelphia City Paper]] |access-date=May 31, 2012}}</ref> Tompkins attended [[Temple University]]; he dropped out<ref name=AVCLUB4>{{Cite web |first=Marah |last=Eakin |date=February 4, 2016 |title=Paul F. Tompkins Wants to Ride a Giant Bison to Work |url=http://www.avclub.com/article/paul-f-tompkins-wants-ride-giant-bison-work-231632 |work=[[The A.V. Club]] |publisher=[[The Onion]] |access-date=June 18, 2016}}</ref> and left for [[Los Angeles]], [[California]], in 1994.<ref name=AVCLUB2/><ref name=CITYPAPER/><ref name=DAILYSHOW>[http://www.thedailyshow.com/news-team/paul-f-tompkins Paul F. Tompkin's bio at TheDailyShow.com]. Retrieved May 31, 2012.</ref>

Tompkins met actor [[Jay Johnston]] in L.A. through their mutual friend, actor and director [[Adam McKay]].<ref name="SOUNDCLOUD">{{cite news |last=Tompkins |first=Paul F. |date=May 28, 2018 |title=SPONTANEANATION 165.5 Bonus: SF Sketchfest Tribute to Paul F. Tompkins |url=https://soundcloud.com/spontaneanation/165-5-bonus-sf-sketchfest}}</ref> McKay and Tompkins had become friends in Philadelphia, where they had both started to perform stand-up at around the same time.<ref name=SFBAYGUARD/><ref name=MNDAILY>{{cite news |title=Paul F. ===Acting and writing===
Tompkins wrote for and performed on ''[[Mr. Show with Bob and David]]'' from 1995 to 1998; the show's writers, including Tompkins, were nominated for an [[Emmy Award]] in 1998 for "Outstanding Writing for a Variety or Music Program".<ref name=AUSTINCH/>

Tompkins's work with ''Mr. Show''<nowiki/>'s creators Bob Odenkirk and David Cross also led to his recurring role on the ''[[Tenacious D (TV series)|Tenacious D]]'' TV series.<ref name=AVCLUB2/><ref name=MNDAILY/> Tompkins played the character of a nightclub manager who is duped into reading Tenacious D's ridiculous introductions during their [[open mic]] performances.<ref name=AVCLUB2/> He revived the role in the comedic band's film ''[[Tenacious D in The Pick of Destiny]]'' released in 2006.

Longtime friend Adam McKay consulted Tompkins regarding the screenplay for ''[[Talladega Nights]]''.<ref name=AVCLUB2/> Tompkins also played the [[Master of Ceremonies|MC]] of a [[cat show]] in McKay's ''[[Anchorman: The Legend of Ron Burgundy]]''.<ref name=DAILYSHOW/><ref name=MNDAILY/><ref name="TALKHUMOR">{{cite web |last=Thorn |first=Simon |date=March 11, 2007 |title=Interview with comedian Paul F. ===Voice acting===
Tompkins has done voice work for many animated television series including ''[[Dr. Katz, Professional Therapist]]'', ''[[King of the Hill]]'', and ''[[Bob's Burgers]]'', in which he voices the recurring character Randy. He lent his voice to a character in an unaired 2007 episode of ''[[Aqua Teen Hunger Force]]'' titled "Boston" that was supposed to be the premiere episode of the show's [[Aqua Teen Hunger Force (season 5)|fifth season]], but it was pulled by [[Turner Broadcasting System]] to avoid further controversy surrounding the [[2007 Boston bomb scare]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.starpulse.com/news/Dee_Doyle/2008/12/15/starpulse_com_exclusive_interview_with_d |title=Exclusive Interview With Meatwad, Er, Dave Willis, Of 'Aqua Teen Hunger Force' |last=Johnson |first=Casey |date=December 15, 2008 |work=starpulse.com |access-date=May 31, 2012 |archive-date=November 15, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101115024706/http://www.starpulse.com/news/Dee_Doyle/2008/12/15/starpulse_com_exclusive_interview_with_d |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Tompkins later appeared in an episode during the show's [[Aqua Teen Hunger Force (season 7)|7th season]]. He was also the voice of one of the thugs in [[Walt Disney Animation Studios]]' 2010 animated film ''[[Tangled]]''. Tompkins was the voice of Benton Criswell, a character in [[MTV]] series ''[[Super Adventure Team]]'' which featured [[marionettes]] in the style of the 1960s British series ''[[Thunderbirds (TV series)|Thunderbirds]]''; the role was credited under the stage name Francis Mt. Pleasant. He was the voice of a puppet in ads for the [[Ford Focus]].<ref name=HUFFPO>{{cite news |title=Paul F. Tompkins Works to Make You Laugh in Laboring Under Delusions |first=Louis |last=Peitzman |url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/louis-peitzman/paul-f-tompkins-interview_b_1439340.html |newspaper=Huffington Post |date=April 20, 2012 |access-date=May 31, 2012}}</ref>

Tompkins played Mr. Peanutbutter in the 2014 Netflix original animated series ''[[BoJack Horseman]]''. Tompkins voices the recurring character, [[Gladstone Gander]], in the [[DuckTales (2017 TV series)|reboot series]] of ''[[DuckTales (2017 TV series)|DuckTales]]''. Tompkins'' with Tompkins as host.<ref name=NYT3/><ref name=AVCLUB1/><ref name=VULTURE2/> From 2006 to 2008, he was a regular guest on ''[[Countdown with Keith Olbermann]]''.<ref name=SFBAYGUARD/><ref name=AVCLUB1/><ref name=IMPOSE/> In 2008, he appeared on ''[[Lewis Black's Root of All Evil]]''<ref name=PRESS1/><ref name=NYPOST>{{cite news |title='Evil' Laugh – Lewis Black's 4-star Farce |first=Linda |last=Stasi |url=http://www.nypost.com/p/entertainment/tv/item_4r97QxSddhV2sPicXGDVjN |newspaper=New York Post |date=March 12, 2008 |access-date=May 31, 2012}}</ref> and took part in a panel on ''[[Larry King Live]]'' in an episode titled "Politics & Humor".

Tompkins has appeared in documentaries such as [[Jamie Kennedy]]'s ''[[Heckler (film)|Heckler]]'' (2007) and [[Doug Benson]]'s ''[[Super High Me]]'' (2007). He also appeared in ''The Bitter Buddha'' (2013), a documentary about the career of actor and comedian [[Eddie Pepitone]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.laughspin.com/2012/03/08/watch-the-bitter-buddha-trailer-with-sarah-silverman-patton-oswalt-more/ |title=Watch the 'Bitter Buddha' trailer with Sarah Silverman, Patton Oswalt, more! |author=Laughspin Staff |date=March 8, 2012 |work=Laughspin |access-date=May 31, 2012 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120310024810/http://www.laughspin.com/2012/03/08/watch-the-bitter-buddha-trailer-with-sarah-silverman-patton-oswalt-more/ |archive-date=March 10, 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=The Bitter Buddha: At 54, Comedian Eddie Pepitone Is Finally Ready for His Close-Up |first=Kristin |last=McCracken |url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/kristin-mccracken/the-bitter-buddha-film_b_2687727.html |newspaper=Huffington Post |date=February 26, 2013 |access-date=March 2, 2013}}</ref>

Tompkins later became the host of a discussion show called ''[[No, You Shut Up!]]'' by [[The Jim Henson Company]] under its Henson Alternative banner.

===Podcasts, webcasts and radio===
In 2010, Tompkins launched his podcast called ''The Pod F. Tompkast''.<ref name=PRESS1/><ref>{{cite podcast |url=http://www.nerdist.com/2010/08/nerdist-podcast-33-paul-f-tompkins/ |title=The Nerdist, Episode #33 |website=nerdist.com |host=Chris Hardwick |date=August 24, 2010 |time=42:03 |access-date=May 31, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120826070310/http://www.nerdist.com/2010/08/nerdist-podcast-33-paul-f-tompkins/ |archive-date=August 26, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The podcast was a mixture of Tompkins discussing various topics, clips from his live show at Largo, and segments where Tompkins voices a variety of celebrities speaking with one another.<ref name=ROLLINGSTONE/><ref name=PRESS1/><ref name=MIDNIGHT>{{cite news |url=http://www.midnightpoutine.ca/theatre/2011/07/just_for_laughs_doubleheader_-_paul_f_tompkins_maria_bamford/ |title=Comedian Paul F. The ''[[Thrilling Adventure Hour]]'' comedy show at Largo began [[podcast]]ing in January 2011; in October of that same year the show's podcasts moved to the Nerdist Industries podcast network created by [[Chris Hardwick]].<ref name="nerdist.com"/> The show ended in 2015.

''[[The Dead Authors Podcast|Dead Authors]]'', a live show that Tompkins hosts at the UCB Theatre in Los Angeles, also began podcasting in September 2011.<ref>[http://thedeadauthorspodcast.libsyn.com/ The Dead Authors Podcast.] Retrieved May 31, 2012</ref>

Bang!]]'' (formerly ''Comedy Death-Ray Radio''),<ref name=SFBAYGUARD/><ref name=SPLITSIDER>{{cite web |url=http://splitsider.com/2011/08/talking-to-paul-f-tompkins-about-podcasting-mr-show-and-how-therapy-improved-his-standup/ |title=Talking to Paul F. Some guests play characters or impersonate certain celebrities, usually for the entirety of the episode; Paul F. Tompkins has impersonated celebrities such as rapper [[Ice-T]], composer [[Andrew Lloyd Webber]], and [[Buddy Valastro]] from the [[reality television]] series ''[[Cake Boss]] (cakeboss.)''.<ref name=SPLITSIDER/>

In addition to Aukerman's ''Comedy Bang! Bang!'', Tompkins has appeared on the podcasts of other fellow comedians such as ''[[WTF with Marc Maron]]'',<ref name=SPLITSIDER/> [[Jimmy Pardo]]'s ''[[Never Not Funny]]'',<ref name="AVCLUB6"/> [[Jessica Chaffin]] and [[Jamie Denbo]]'s ''[[Ronna and Beverly]]'' podcast,<ref name=SPLITSIDER/> and the ''[[Superego (podcast)|Superego]]'' podcast with [[Jeremy Carter]], [[Matt Gourley]], and Mark McConville.<ref name=AUSTINIST>{{cite web |url=http://austinist.com/2012/05/23/paul_f_tompkins_a_fancy_man.php |title=An Interview with Paul F. Tompkins: A Very Fancy Man |last=Brumby |first=Arian |date=May 23, 2012 |work=Austinist |publisher=Gothamist |access-date=May 31, 2012}}</ref> Tompkins has also been a regular guest on the radio show and podcast ''[[The Best Show on WFMU with Tom Scharpling]]''.<ref name=SPLITSIDER/><ref name="AVCLUB6" />

In 2015, Tompkins created his own podcast on the [[Earwolf]] podcast network called ''[[Spontaneanation |Spontaneanation with Paul F. Tompkins]]''. This podcast is similar to the ''Pod F. Tompkast''; however, ''Spontaneanation'' is fully improvised and in-the-moment, as opposed to the ''Tompkast'', which was highly produced. ''Spontaneanation'' begins with an improvised monologue, accompanied on piano by Eban Schletter, much like the ''Pod F. Tompkast''. The next segment is an interview with one of Tompkins's famous friends. The final segment is one long improvised story performed by Paul and guest improvisers, based on ideas discussed in the interview segment. The podcast ended in 2019.

Since 2019, Tompkins has co-hosted, with [[Nicole Parker]], ''The Neighborhood Listen'' on Stitcher Premium. Along with [[Tawny Newsome]], he also hosts ''The Pod Directive'', the official Star Trek podcast, which launched in September 2020  

Since 2018, Paul has co-hosted with Scott Aukerman and Lauren Lapkus the podcast Threedom. 

In March 2020, during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Tompkins started a weekly podcast with his wife, Janie Haddad Tompkins, called ''Stay F. Homekins''.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=April 9, 2020 |title=This Week in Comedy Podcasts: Remember to Stay F. Homekins |url=https://www.vulture.com/2020/04/this-week-in-comedy-podcasts-remember-to-stay-f-homekins.html |access-date=March 15, 2021 |website=Vulture |language=en-us}}</ref> The first season ran for 41 episodes throughout the rest of 2020, and season two started in January 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Stay F. Homekins: with Janie Haddad Tompkins & Paul F. Tompkins |url=https://stayfhomekins.buzzsprout.com/938197 |access-date=March 15, 2021 |website=Buzzsprout}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Tompkins is married to actress Janie Haddad Tompkins, who is best known for voicing the red anthropomorphic cardinal Margaret on ''[[Regular Show]]''.<ref>{{cite news |title=Paul F. In 2017, Tompkins stated on [[Twitter]] that he was once a [[Catholic Church|Catholic]], but later went on to become an atheist.<ref>{{cite web |title=I am a former Catholic who is now an atheist who doesn't see the value in calling people of faith stupid. |url=https://twitter.com/PFTompkins/status/870738558239203329 |access-date=March 10, 2019 |website=Twitter}}</ref>

He is a member of the [[Democratic Socialists of America]] and helped canvass for [[Eunisses Hernandez]] and [[Hugo Soto-Martinez]] during the [[2022 Los Angeles elections]].<ref>{{cite tweet|number=1531621516072337412|user=DSA_LosAngeles|title=Time to announce TONIGHT'S final surprise guest! It's Paul F. Tompkins (@PFTompkins) himself! Join us (and a bevy of others!) at our RALLY FOR LA fundraiser in support of @HugoForCD13 & @EunissesH at the Teragram Ballroom at 7PM! 🎟 Grab your tix at http://dsa-la.org/rallyforLA 🎫|date=May 31, 2022|author=Democratic Socialists of America}}</ref>
