'''Nolan North''' (born October 31, 1970)<ref>{{cite AV media |date=October 31, 2019 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HIrI-lPsvcU |title=Nolan North and Troy Baker aren't Scared in the Scary Silent HiIl |publisher=CouchSoup |via=[[YouTube]] |access-date=December 7, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220420121429/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HIrI-lPsvcU |archive-date=April 20, 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref> is an American actor best known for his voice acting roles.

After his breakthrough role as Dr. Chris Ramsey on the [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] soap opera ''[[Port Charles]]'' in 1997, North moved into voice acting when the show ended in 2003 and has since become best known for his video game roles as [[Nathan Drake]] in the ''[[Uncharted]]'' series, [[Desmond Miles]] in the ''[[Assassin's Creed]]'' series, Merasmus in ''[[Team Fortress 2]]'', [[Prince (Prince of Persia)|the Prince]] in ''[[Prince of Persia (2008 video game)|Prince of Persia]]'', Dr. Edward Richtofen in the ''[[Call of Duty]]'' franchise, [[Deadpool]] in various [[Marvel Comics]] media, the [[Penguin (character)|Penguin]] in the ''[[Batman: Arkham]]'' franchise, [[Captain Martin Walker]] in ''[[Spec Ops: The Line]]'', [[Characters of The Last of Us#David|David]] in ''[[The Last of Us (video game)|The Last of Us]]'', himself as one of the voices for the player character in ''[[Saints Row IV]]'', [[Iron Man]] in ''[[Marvel's Avengers (video game)|Marvel's Avengers]]'', and Ghost in the [[Destiny (video game series)|''Destiny'' video game series]].

In animation, North voices [[Smokescreen (Transformers)|Smokescreen]] on ''[[Transformers: Prime]]'', [[Conner Kent|Superboy]] on ''[[Young Justice (TV series)|Young Justice]]'', and the titular character in ''[[Blaze and the Monster Machines]]''.

== Early life ==
North was born on October 31, 1970, in [[New Haven, Connecticut]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://familysearch.org/search/record/results?count=20&query=+givenname:%22Nolan+Ramsey%22~++surname:North~|title=FamilySearch|website=familysearch.org|access-date=July 23, 2018|archive-date=April 20, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220420121359/https://www.familysearch.org/search/record/results?count=20&query=+givenname:%22Nolan+Ramsey%22~++surname:North~|url-status=live}}</ref> and raised in [[Warwick, Rhode Island]], where he attended and played baseball at [[Bishop Hendricken High School]].<ref>{{cite tweet |last=North |first=Nolan |author-link=Nolan North |user=nolan_north |number=610841172659957760 |date=June 16, 2015 |title="@SoSofieFatale: @nolan_north did you go to high school in RI by chance?" Yep! Bishop Hendricken. |language=en |access-date=December 7, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220426141431/https://twitter.com/nolan_north/status/610841172659957760 |archive-date=April 26, 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref> He majored in journalism with a baseball scholarship at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]],<ref name="PCBio">{{cite web |url=http://www.soapcentral.com/pc/theactors/north.php |title=Soap Central bio |work=Soap Central |access-date=June 3, 2011 |archive-date=March 24, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100324184311/http://www.soapcentral.com/pc/theactors/north.php |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="GamePro">{{cite magazine |url=http://www.gamepro.com/article/features/213578/the-man-behind-nathan-drake-i-get-paid-to-do-what-used-to-get-me-detention/ |title=The man behind Nathan Drake |author=Blake Snow |date=January 14, 2010 |magazine=Gamepro |access-date=June 3, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100926214839/http://www.gamepro.com/article/features/213578/the-man-behind-nathan-drake-i-get-paid-to-do-what-used-to-get-me-detention/|archive-date=September 26, 2010}}</ref> and spent the next year working as a reporter in [[New Jersey]] before moving to New York City to pursue a career in stand-up comedy and acting.<ref name="PCBio" />

== Career ==
North eventually relocated to Los Angeles, where he was cast as Dr. Chris Ramsey in the ''[[General Hospital]]'' spin-off series ''[[Port Charles]]'' in 1997.<ref name="GamePro" /> He worked as a voice actor on a few video games during this time, and began to focus on this career path following the cancellation of ''Port Charles'' in 2003.<ref name="GamePro" />

One of North's most notable voice roles came in 2007, when he voiced and performed [[motion-capture acting|motion capture]] for the protagonist [[Nathan Drake]] in the video game ''[[Uncharted: Drake's Fortune]]''. Since then, he has continued to portray the character in ''[[Uncharted 2: Among Thieves]]'' (2009), ''[[Uncharted 3: Drake's Deception]]'' (2011), and '' [[Uncharted 4: A Thief's End]]'' (2016),<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2014/12/06/psx-2014-uncharted-4-gameplay-shows-off-new-mechanics |title=PSX 2014: Uncharted 4 Gameplay Shows Off New Mechanics – IGN |date=December 6, 2014 |publisher=IGN |access-date=December 6, 2014 |archive-date=December 8, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141208014812/http://www.ign.com/articles/2014/12/06/psx-2014-uncharted-4-gameplay-shows-off-new-mechanics |url-status=live }}</ref> as well as the [[PlayStation Vita]] exclusive ''[[Uncharted: Golden Abyss]]'' (2012). In an interview with ''[[The Guardian]]'', he said his time as Drake requires "a lot of imagination" because "motion capture is basically theatre in [[spandex]]; there's minimal props, and you need a willingness to make an ass of yourself".<ref name="GuardianInterview" /> For his role as Drake, North was twice nominated at the [[Spike Video Game Awards]] in the "Best Performance by a Human Male" category.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gamerant.com/2011-spike-video-game-awards-complete-winners-list/ |title=2011 Spike Video Game Awards: Complete Winners List |last=Keyes |first=Rob |date=December 10, 2011 |website=Game Rant |access-date=December 10, 2011 |archive-date=February 7, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200207041839/https://gamerant.com/2011-spike-video-game-awards-complete-winners-list/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

North's other notable video game voice roles include the Prince in ''[[Prince of Persia (2008 video game)|Prince of Persia]]'' and Desmond Miles in the ''[[Assassin's Creed]]'' series. He also voiced Vossler in ''[[Final Fantasy XII]]'', Eradan in ''[[Lord of the Rings: War in the North]]'', the male Jedi Consular in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' and its following expansions, [[Characters of The Last of Us#David|David]] in ''[[The Last of Us (video game)|The Last of Us]]'', Dr. Edward Richtofen in the [[Call of Duty Zombies|”Zombies” mode]] of the ''[[Call of Duty]]'' series, [[List of Transformers film series cast and characters#Brawl|Brawl]] in ''[[Transformers: War for Cybertron]]'', and [[Ghost Rider (Johnny Blaze)|Ghost Rider]] in ''[[Marvel: Ultimate Alliance]]'', as well as Shadow Demon, Lycan, Lone Druid, Brewmaster, Gyrocopter, Ogre Magi, Meepo, Earth Spirit, Troll Warlord, and the Keeper of the Light in ''[[Dota 2]]''. He voices various ''[[Team Fortress 2]]'' characters such as the Engineer (partially), Merasmus, Redmond Mann, Blutarch Mann, Zepheniah Mann, and the Bombinomicon. He also replaced [[Peter Dinklage]] as the voice of the Ghost in ''[[Destiny: The Taken King]]'', and additionally re-recorded all of Dinklage's lines from the base game ''[[Destiny (video game)|Destiny]]''. He continues to voice the character in subsequent releases. Following the release of ''[[Destiny 2: Forsaken]]'', he portrayed not only Ghost but also took over the role of Cayde-6 from [[Nathan Fillion]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Kain |first=Erik |date=July 17, 2018 |title=Nathan Fillion Isn't Voicing Cayde-6 In Destiny 2's 'Forsaken' DLC |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/erikkain/2018/07/17/nathan-fillion-isnt-voicing-cayde-6-in-destiny-2s-forsaken-dlc/?sh=6dcdcbcb21e4 |work=[[Forbes]] |access-date=July 17, 2018 |archive-date=April 14, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210414203206/https://www.forbes.com/sites/erikkain/2018/07/17/nathan-fillion-isnt-voicing-cayde-6-in-destiny-2s-forsaken-dlc/?sh=6dcdcbcb21e4 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In the 2013 film ''[[Star Trek Into Darkness]]'', North made one of his few increasingly rare live-action appearances since becoming a voice actor. Director [[J. J. Abrams]] had cited North's performance as Drake in the decision to cast him as a starship helmsman, as he and his son are fans of the ''Uncharted'' series.<ref name="Nolan_North_Star_Trek" /> In a May 2012 interview, North said, "[Abrams is] a huge fan of gaming and he was telling me how people just don't understand [the medium] yet, but they're going to catch up. They don't understand how amazing this technology is and it doesn't get the respect it deserves, but if it keeps making the money it makes you're going to see more and more people converted. I mean, [[Gary Oldman]], one of the greatest actors on the planet, did ''[[Call of Duty: World at War|Call of Duty]]''. He wouldn't have done it 10 years ago. It's a new age dawning, and I'm just really proud to be part of it."<ref name="Nolan_North_Star_Trek" />

North's animation roles include the voices of [[Cyclops (Marvel Comics)|Cyclops]] in ''[[Wolverine and the X-Men (TV series)|Wolverine and the X-Men]]'', [[Snow Job (G.I. Joe)|Snow Job]] in ''[[G.I. Joe: Renegades]]'', [[Raphael (Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles)|Raphael]] in ''[[TMNT (film)|TMNT]]'', both [[Conner Kent|Superboy]] and [[Superman]] in ''[[Young Justice (TV series)|Young Justice]]'', and [[Smokescreen (Transformers)|Smokescreen]] in ''[[Transformers: Prime]]''. He has also voiced Blaze in ''[[Blaze and the Monster Machines]]'' since 2014. He was honored at a special event hosted by the [[British Academy of Film and Television Arts]] during the [[Electronic Entertainment Expo 2018|2018 EA Expo]], where he was given a special award for "outstanding contribution to performance in games".<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.bafta.org/media-centre/press-releases/games-special-award-2018 | title = BAFTA to Honour Nolan North with Special Award | date = May 11, 2018 | access-date = May 11, 2018 | publisher = [[British Academy of Film and Television Arts]] | archive-date = May 11, 2018 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180511215008/http://www.bafta.org/media-centre/press-releases/games-special-award-2018 | url-status = live }}</ref>

In April 2018, North began hosting ''Retro Replay'' with fellow voice actor and frequent co-star [[Troy Baker]]. The show, which featured the two playing games in which they were involved while giving behind-the-scenes commentary on the making of the games, partnered with [[Rooster Teeth]] in April 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Exclusive: Nolan North and Troy Baker take 'convention circuit'-born Retro Replay to Rooster Teeth|url=https://www.syfy.com/syfywire/exclusive-nolan-north-troy-baker-retro-replay-rooster-teeth|last=Oller|first=Jacob|date=April 24, 2019|website=SYFY WIRE|language=en|access-date=May 16, 2020|archive-date=June 15, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200615113054/https://www.syfy.com/syfywire/exclusive-nolan-north-troy-baker-retro-replay-rooster-teeth|url-status=live}}</ref> Baker left ''Retro Replay'' in April 2020, due to an apparent disagreement on the future direction of the series.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Troy Baker has left Retro Replay|url=https://www.gamereactor.eu/troy-baker-has-left-retro-replay/|last=Hirsilä|first=Markus|website=Gamereactor UK|date=April 23, 2020 |language=en|access-date=May 16, 2020|archive-date=March 8, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210308131505/https://www.gamereactor.eu/troy-baker-has-left-retro-replay/|url-status=live}}</ref> The following month, North announced that the series was ending its partnership with Rooster Teeth.<ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tj46NNMaifY&t=2m2s | archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211108/tj46NNMaifY| archive-date=November 8, 2021 | url-status=live|title=Nolan North Live From Quarantine! |last=North |first=Nolan |work=Retro Replay |time=2:02 |date=May 7, 2020 |access-date=May 18, 2020 }}{{cbignore}}</ref> He had a brief cameo in the 2022 ''[[Uncharted (film)|Uncharted]]'' film adaptation and also narrated the audiobook edition.<ref name=Unchartedaudiobook>{{cite web|last=Moreau|first=Jordan|date=February 9, 2022|url=https://variety.com/2022/digital/news/uncharted-nolan-north-book-1235175555/|title='Uncharted' Audio Book to Be Narrated by Voice Actor Nolan North (EXCLUSIVE)|publisher=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|accessdate=February 18, 2017|archive-date=February 9, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209215434/https://variety.com/2022/digital/news/uncharted-nolan-north-book-1235175555/|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2024, he appeared as Gene Campbell in the [[Peacock (streaming service)|Peacock]] television series ''[[Hysteria!]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2024/02/garret-dillahunt-nolan-north-cast-peacock-satanic-panic-series-hysteria-1235840792/|title=Garret Dillahunt, Nolan North, Elijah Richardson Among 6 Cast In Peacock's Satanic Panic Thriller Series 'Hysteria!'|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|first=Denise|last=Petski|date=February 28, 2024|access-date=November 29, 2024|archive-date=September 12, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240912110720/https://deadline.com/2024/02/garret-dillahunt-nolan-north-cast-peacock-satanic-panic-series-hysteria-1235840792/|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
North married his ''Port Charles'' co-star Jill Murray on June 4, 1999.<ref name="PCBio" /> They have two children together.<ref name="PCBio" /><ref>{{Cite web|url = https://grantland.com/hollywood-prospectus/the-hidden-king-meet-nolan-north-the-biggest-voice-in-video-games/|title = The Hidden King: Meet Nolan North, the Biggest Voice in Video Games|date = September 15, 2015|access-date = May 21, 2020|archive-date = June 6, 2020|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200606160051/http://grantland.com/hollywood-prospectus/the-hidden-king-meet-nolan-north-the-biggest-voice-in-video-games/|url-status = live|author-first1=Ben|author-last1=Lindbergh}}</ref>

He also acted in another production in the same year at Fullerton College called ''Red Noses'', a [[black comedy]] produced by [[Peter Barnes (playwright)|Peter Barnes]] and directed by [[Michael Fields (director)|Michael Fields]].{{cite news|title=Fullerton College Lacks Breadth for Black Comedy 'Red Noses'|work=Los Angeles Times|date=1990-06-19|author=Smith, Mark Chalon}} Williams has appeared on many TV series since 1994, including ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'', ''[[Beverly Hills, 90210]]'', ''[[NYPD Blue]]'', ''[[Lois & Clark: The New Adventures of Superman]]'', ''[[JAG (TV series)|JAG]]'', ''[[Living Single]]'', ''[[Nash Bridges]]'', ''[[Providence (American TV series)|Providence]]'', ''[[Law & Order: Special Victims Unit]]'', ''[[Veronica Mars]]'', ''[[The West Wing]]'', ''[[Close to Home (2005 TV series)|Close to Home]]'', ''[[ER (TV series)|ER]]'', and ''[[Grey's Anatomy]]''. He was the fifth cast member in the original pilot for ''[[Will & Grace]]'', playing Will's law firm partner, but was dropped during rehearsals because director Jim Burrows said they didn't need his character.{{cite web |title=Paley Celebrates Pride: Will & Grace at PaleyFest LA: Full Conversation | website=[[YouTube]] | date=10 June 2020 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lfyawsvnEYk |access-date=21 January 2023 |language=en}} He portrayed [[List of minor recurring characters in Star Trek: Deep Space Nine|Talak'talan]], a [[Jem'Hadar]] leader in the Star Trek series, in a ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'' episode "[[The Jem'Hadar]]".{{cite web|access-date=2008-10-04|url=http://www.startrek.com/startrek/view/series/DS9/episode/68174.html|title=The Jem'Hadar|publisher=Star Trek|archive-date=2008-08-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080820113453/http://www.startrek.com/startrek/view/series/DS9/episode/68174.html|url-status=dead}} Williams joined the ''[[Prison Break]]'' cast by playing [[The Company (Prison Break)|The Company]]'s assassin, Wyatt Mathewson.{{cite web|url=http://www.prisonbreakbuff.com/2008/06/04/cress-williams-to-join-prison-break-season-4-as-assassin/|title=Cress Williams to Join Prison Break Season 4 as Assassin|access-date=2008-06-04|author=Nikki|publisher=Prison Break Buff|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080605120329/http://www.prisonbreakbuff.com/2008/06/04/cress-williams-to-join-prison-break-season-4-as-assassin/|archive-date=2008-06-05}} He appeared in the final season of ''[[Friday Night Lights (TV series)|Friday Night Lights]]'' as Ornette Howard, father of East Dillon's star quarterback Vince Howard. After his ''Black Lightning'' series concluded, he reprised the role on ''[[The Flash (2014 TV series)|The Flash]]'' at the start of its eighth season as part of its "Armageddon" event.{{cite web |last1=Del Rosario |first1=Alexandra |title='The Flash': Lineup of Superheroes & Villains Revealed For 5-Part Season 8 Launch Event |url=https://deadline.com/2021/08/the-flash-lineup-of-superheroes-villains-revealed-for-5-part-season-8-launch-event-1234821825/ |website=Deadline |access-date=7 October 2021 |date=25 August 2021}} == Personal life == On October 14, 2000, Williams married actress [[Simbi Khali]] in [[Malibu, California]].{{cite journal|date=November 27, 2000|title=Wed|url=http://people.com/archive/passages-vol-54-no-22/|department=Passages|publisher=[[Time Inc.]]|volume=54|issue=22|access-date=February 11, 2018|journal=[[People (magazine)|People]]}} The couple had two children and divorced in 2011. [[University College London]] | occupation = | spouse = | parents = | children = }} '''Harry George Judge''' (1 August 1928 – 2 April 2019) was senior research fellow at the [[Department of Education, University of Oxford]] and emeritus fellow of [[Brasenose College, Oxford]].{{cite web | url = http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U22561 | title = JUDGE, Harry George | access-date = 17 August 2012 | year = 2011 | work = [[Who's Who (UK)|Who's Who]] 2012 | publisher = Oxford University Press}}{{cite web |url=https://www.bnc.ox.ac.uk/about-brasenose/news/2088-dr-harry-judge-an-appreciation |title=Dr Harry Judge: An Appreciation |work=News |publisher=Brasenose College, Oxford |access-date=2019-04-05 }} He was director of the Department of Educational Studies from 1973 to 1988.{{cite web | url = http://www.education.ox.ac.uk/about-us/directory/dr-harry-judge/ | title = Dr Harry Judge | access-date = 17 August 2012 | publisher = Department of Education, [[University of Oxford]]}} His 80th birthday was marked by the publication of a special volume of the Oxford Review of Education.{{cite journal | title = Making a difference: Harry Judge, teacher education, the university, and the schools | journal = Oxford Review of Education | date = June 2008 | first = Phillips | last = David | volume = 34 | issue = 3 | pages = 271–4 | doi = 10.1080/03054980802116816 }} He was the honorary president of the Oxford Education Society.{{cite web | url = http://www.oxes.org.uk/about-us/who-are-we/ | title = Oxford Education Society: Your Committee | access-date = 28 August 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120710033452/http://www.oxes.org.uk/about-us/who-are-we/ | archive-date = 10 July 2012 | url-status = dead }} Born in Cardiff, after two years in the [[Royal Air Force]] he studied at Brasenose College, taking degrees in [[Modern History]] and in [[Theology]].{{cite news |last=Roberts |first=James |url=https://www.oxfordmail.co.uk/news/17583276.obituary-dr-harry-judge-of-brasenose-college-and-banbury-school/ |title=OBITUARY: Dr Harry Judge, of Brasenose College and Banbury School |work=[[Oxford Mail]] |date=2019-04-18 |access-date=2019-04-20 }} While teaching in schools in [[London]] and [[Surrey]] he completed a Ph.D. in French history and in 1959 was invited to become director of studies at the St Katharine’s Foundation, [[Cumberland Lodge]].{{cite book |last=Reeves |first1=Marjorie |title=Christian thinking and social order: conviction politics from the 1930s to the present day |location=London |publisher=Cassell |date=1999 |isbn=0304702471 }} In 1962, he was appointed Headmaster of Banbury Grammar School and coordinated its merger with three other secondary schools to form Banbury School (now [[Wykham Park Academy]]), of which he became the first principal.{{cite book |last=Crossman |first1=Richard |author-link=Richard Crossman |title=The Diaries of a Cabinet Minister |volume=1 |publisher=Hamish Hamilton |date=1975 |isbn=0241891108 |url-access=registration |url=https://archive.org/details/diariesofcabinet0000cros }} While in Banbury, he was a member of the Public Schools Commissions{{cite book |last=Newsom |first1=John |title=The Public Schools Commission first report |location=London |publisher=[[Office of Public Sector Information|HMSO]] |year=1968 |isbn=0112700012 }}{{cite book |last=Newsom |first1=John |title=The Public Schools Commission second report |location=London |publisher=[[Office of Public Sector Information|HMSO]] |year=1970 |isbn=0112701701 }} and in 1970 of the James Committee of Enquiry into Teacher Education.{{cite book |last=James |first1=Eric |author-link=Eric James, Baron James of Rusholme |title=Teacher education and training |location=London |publisher=[[Office of Public Sector Information|HMSO]] |year=1972 |isbn=0112702368 }} In 1973, he was elected as director of the Oxford University Department of Educational Studies (later to be renamed the Department of Education) and a professorial fellow of Brasenose College. His work at Oxford focused on building a research partnership extending across the university and on integrating the university role with that of local schools in the professional education of teachers.{{cite book |last=Benton |first1=Peter |title=The Oxford internship scheme : integration + partnership in initial teacher education |location=London |publisher=[[Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation]] |year=1990 |isbn=0903319535 }} In the 1980s he chaired the [[BBC School Radio|BBC Schools Broadcasting Council]] and the [[Royal College of Nursing]] [[Judge Report|Commission on the education of nurses]].{{cite book |last=Commission on Nursing Education |title=The education of nurses |location=London |publisher=[[Royal College of Nursing]] |year=1985 }} He completed for the [[Ford Foundation]] a report on graduate schools of education in the United States, and on his retirement from his Oxford appointments became professor of teacher education policy at [[Michigan State University]], subsequently serving as a senior scholar at the [[Carnegie Foundation for the Advancement of Teaching]] at [[Stanford University]]. ==Selected publications== * ''Oxford Illustrated '' '''Jason Mantzoukas''' ({{IPAc-en|m|æ|n|ˈ|z|uː|k|ə|s}}; born December 18, 1972) is an American actor, comedian, podcaster and screenwriter. He is known for his roles as Rafi in the [[FX (TV channel)|FX]] comedy series ''[[The League]]'' and as Nadal in [[Sacha Baron Cohen]]'s ''[[The Dictator]]'' (2012), and he is one of the three co-hosts of the podcast ''[[How Did This Get Made?]]'' alongside [[Paul Scheer]] and [[June Diane Raphael]].

After beginning his career as an improv comedian, he has played several comedic roles in film and television. He appeared in the films ''[[Conception (film)|Conception]]'' (2011), ''[[They Came Together]]'' (2014), ''[[Sleeping with Other People]]'' (2015), ''[[The Long Dumb Road]]'' (2018), and ''[[John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum]]'' (2019). He has had recurring roles on four TV series created by [[Michael Schur]], portraying Dennis Feinstein in ''[[Parks and Recreation]]'', Adrian Pimento in [[Brooklyn Nine-Nine]], Derek Hoffstetler in ''[[The Good Place]]'', and Apollo Lambrakis in ''[[A Man on the Inside]]''. In 2025, he appeared as a contestant in series 19 of British comedy game show ''[[Taskmaster (TV series)|Taskmaster]]''.

Mantzoukas also voices the characters Jay Bilzerian in the [[Netflix]] animated series ''[[Big Mouth (American TV series)|Big Mouth]]'', Alex Dorpenberger in the [[HBO Max]] animated series ''[[Close Enough]]'', [[Rex Splode]] in the [[Amazon Prime]] animated series ''[[Invincible (TV series)|Invincible]]'', The Gray One in ''[[HouseBroken]]'', Chumsley in ''[[Gabby's Dollhouse: The Movie]]'', and Jankom Pog in the [[Paramount+]] animated series ''[[Star Trek: Prodigy]]''.

==Early life and education==
Mantzoukas was born December 18, 1972,<ref name="IMDb"/><ref>{{cite web|title=Jason Mantzoukas - Fandango|url=https://www.fandango.com/people/jason-mantzoukas-424276/biography |website=Fandango}}</ref> in [[Lynn, Massachusetts]]. At the age of four, his family moved to [[Nahant, Massachusetts|Nahant]], a town nearby to Lynn.<ref>[https://www.nshoremag.com/faces-places/interview-with-jason-mantzoukas/ Interview with Jason Mantzoukas]</ref> He is the oldest child of Cynthia (née Mourousas) and William Mantzoukas, second-generation [[Greek Americans|Greek-Americans]].<ref name="northshore">{{cite news|url=https://www.nshoremag.com/faces-places/interview-with-jason-mantzoukas |first=Beth|last=Daigle|date=December 13, 2018|title=Interview with Jason Mantzoukas|work=nshoremag.com|access-date=April 24, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/jason-mantzoukas/bio/673037/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811104857/http://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/jason-mantzoukas/bio/673037/|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 11, 2017|title=Jason Mantzoukas Biography|website=[[TV Guide]]}}</ref> He has one younger sister, Melissa.<ref>{{cite news|first=Ellen |last=Gamerman |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/jason-mantzoukas-breaks-out-in-the-house-1498059098 |title=Now Starring With Will Ferrell and Amy Poehler: This Guy? |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |date=June 21, 2017}}</ref> He has described himself as "100 percent [[Greeks|Greek]]".<ref name="entertainmentweekly"/><ref name="straight">{{cite news|last=Jones|first=Patty| url=https://www.straight.com/article-679936/vancouver/dictator-wields-comic-arsenal|title=The Dictator wields a comic arsenal|work=[[The Georgia Straight]]|date=May 9, 2012|access-date=October 12, 2013}}</ref>

Mantzoukas began taking drum lessons at age 10 and studied under Steve Barrett for over 8 years.<ref>{{cite podcast |url=https://armchairexpertpod.com/pods/jason-mantzoukas |title=Jason Mantzoukas |website=[[Armchair Expert]] |publisher=[[Stitcher Radio]] |host=[[Dax Shepard]], Monica Padman |date=February 11, 2019 |time=33:55 }}</ref> In interviews, he has cited [[Stewart Copeland]], [[Stephen Perkins]] from [[Jane's Addiction]], and [[Jimmy Chamberlin]] from [[The Smashing Pumpkins]] as his biggest influences as a young musician.<ref>{{cite podcast |url=https://armchairexpertpod.com/pods/jason-mantzoukas |title=Jason Mantzoukas |website=[[Armchair Expert]] |publisher=[[Stitcher Radio]] |host=[[Dax Shepard]], Monica Padman |date=February 11, 2019 |time=34:49 }}</ref> He participated in jazz and marching bands in high school, as well as playing in a cover band called Slygoul.<ref>{{cite web |last=dharmachine |url=https://blog.discogs.com/en/essential-wax-jason-mantzoukas/ |title=Jason Mantzoukas' Top Five 'Beach' Records |work=Discogs Blog |date=July 2, 2019}}</ref> He continued with jazz drumming in college and played for a [[bebop]] group.<ref name="Offer inter">{{cite news|first=Nick |last=Offerman |title= Kings of Comedy: Jason Mantzoukas by Nick Offerman |url=https://www.interviewmagazine.com/culture/jason-mantzoukas-by-nick-offerman |work=[[Interview (magazine)|Interview]] |date=November 9, 2014}}</ref>

Mantzoukas attended [[Swampscott High School]], graduating in 1991.<ref>{{cite web |title=Shrewsbury: David Dragonetti Q&A |url=https://www.redbankgreen.com/2018/11/shrewsbury-david-dragonetti/ |work=redbankgreen |date=November 2, 2018 |quote=I graduated from Swampscott High School...in 1991. Notable graduates include... actor/comedian Jason Mantzoukas.}}</ref> While attending, he was named captain of Swampscott's boys' soccer and track teams and was president of the marching band.<ref>{{cite podcast |url=https://www.earwolf.com/episode/space-jam-live/ |title=Space Jam: LIVE! |website=[[How Did This Get Made?]] |publisher=[[Earwolf]] |host1=[[Paul Scheer]] |host2=Jason Mantzoukas |host3=[[June Diane Raphael]] |date=February 13, 2020 |time=50:24 }}</ref> He attended [[Middlebury College]] in [[Middlebury, Vermont]], where he majored in religion.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.middlebury.edu/giving/difference/toolkit/Arts|title=Arts Middlebury|website=[[Middlebury College]]|access-date=August 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005184759/http://www.middlebury.edu/giving/difference/toolkit/Arts|archive-date=October 5, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He attempted to defend a "terribly written" honors thesis on [[religious iconography]] (which he admits to starting a week prior to his defense date) but was not given credit to graduate with honors.<ref name="maron">{{cite podcast |url=http://www.wtfpod.com/podcast/episode-824-jason-mantzoukas |title=Episode 824 - Jason Mantzoukas |website=[[WTF with Marc Maron]] |host=[[Marc Maron]] |date=June 27, 2017 }}</ref>

After graduating from college in 1995, Mantzoukas was granted a [[Watson Foundation#Thomas J. Watson Fellowship|Watson Fellowship]] and traveled throughout North Africa and the Middle East studying religious and transcendental music for nearly two years.<ref name="entertainmentweekly">{{cite magazine |last=Rottenberg |first=Jason |url=https://www.ew.com/article/2012/05/18/dictators-jason-mantzoukas |title=The Dictator's Jason Mantzoukas |date=May 18, 2012 |magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150507192142/https://www.ew.com/article/2012/05/18/dictators-jason-mantzoukas |access-date=August 2, 2016 |archive-date=May 7, 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.vulture.com/2017/06/the-improvised-life-of-jason-mantzoukas.html |first= Ian |last= Goldstein |title=Improvising Through Life with Jason Mantzoukas |work=[[New York (magazine)#Digital|Vulture]] |date=June 28, 2017 |access-date=December 17, 2018}}</ref> He has admitted to having a "horrible [grant proposal] but was charming in the room; so [he earned the grant]."<ref name="maron"/> At the time he left for Morocco for the Watson Fellowship, he had already had six auditions and callbacks for the [[Blue Man Group]], but he ultimately decided to travel before the audition process was complete.<ref>{{cite news |first=Michael |last=Riedel |title=Learning the Blues |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/learning-blues-article-1.720431 |work=[[New York Daily News]] |date=February 4, 1996 |quote=...Jason Mantzoukas. A 23-year-old student at Middlebury College, Mantzoukas drove down from Vermont this morning for the audition.}}</ref><ref>{{cite podcast |url=https://omny.fm/shows/comedy-bang-bang-the-podcast/jason-mantzoukas-thomas-middleditch#description |title=Jason Mantzoukas, Thomas Middleditch |website= |host=[[Scott Aukerman]] |date=November 2, 2020 |time=35:52 |access-date=January 10, 2021 |archive-date=January 11, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210111213744/https://omny.fm/shows/comedy-bang-bang-the-podcast/jason-mantzoukas-thomas-middleditch#description |url-status=dead }}</ref> He lived in [[Morocco]] for about 7½ months while studying and recording [[Gnawa music]].<ref>{{cite podcast |url=https://armchairexpertpod.com/pods/jason-mantzoukas |title=Jason Mantzoukas |website=[[Armchair Expert]] |publisher=[[Stitcher Radio]] |host=[[Dax Shepard]], Monica Padman |date=February 11, 2019 |time= 53:24}}</ref> While abroad, he traveled to [[Egypt]], [[Israel]], [[Turkey]], [[Jordan]], and [[Syria]].<ref name="maron"/> During his time abroad, he was arrested once in Morocco, for having an expired tourist visa, and in Turkey to prevent him from traveling through an active war zone.<ref name="maron"/>

==Career==
===Early comedy===
Mantzoukas first began writing comedy sketches during his junior and senior years of high school for variety shows.<ref name="jester">{{cite web|url=http://www.jesterjournal.com/IntMantzoukas.htm |title=The Jester Interview: Jason Mantzoukas|last=Shashoua|first=Michael|website=The Jester Journal}}</ref> He began performing short-form [[improvisational comedy]] (improv) as a part of the Otter Nonsense Players at Middlebury College and became "obsessed" with improv as it used the same skill set as performing [[jazz]].<ref name="maron"/> While performing with the Otters, Mantzoukas met and began learning and practicing long-form improv with fellow performers, [[Jessica St. Clair]], [[Dan O'Brien (playwright)|Dan O'Brien]], and [[Rodney Rothman]].<ref name="Offer inter"/>

===Upright Citizens Brigade===
After moving to New York City in 1998, he began performing comedy regularly at the [[Upright Citizens Brigade Theater]] (UCB) and was taught by [[Amy Poehler]].<ref name="Offer inter"/> He was a member of the improv team "Mother", one of the UCB's earliest house teams.<ref name="jester"/><ref>{{cite podcast |url=https://armchairexpertpod.com/pods/jason-mantzoukas |title=Jason Mantzoukas |website=[[Armchair Expert]] |publisher=[[Stitcher Radio]] |host=[[Dax Shepard]], Monica Padman |date=February 11, 2019 |time=1:19:15 }}</ref><ref>{{cite podcast |url=https://armchairexpertpod.com/pods/jason-mantzoukas |title=Jason Mantzoukas |website=[[Armchair Expert]] |publisher=[[Stitcher Radio]] |host=[[Dax Shepard]], Monica Padman |date=February 11, 2019 |time=1:06:10 }}</ref> During his time at UCB, Mantzoukas worked in the computer graphics department at [[J. P. Morgan]] for over three years to "make ends meet."<ref>{{cite podcast |url=https://armchairexpertpod.com/pods/jason-mantzoukas |title=Jason Mantzoukas |website=[[Armchair Expert]] |publisher=[[Stitcher Radio]] |host=[[Dax Shepard]], Monica Padman |date=February 11, 2019 |time=1:08:06}}</ref>

Mantzoukas and comedian Ed Herbstman performed as the comedy duo "The Mantzoukas Brothers" for a number of years and were named the "Best Improv Duo" by ''[[Time Out New York]]'' magazine in 2006.<ref name="jester"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://bestnewyorkcomedy.com/tag/the-mantzoukas-brothers/|title=The Mantzoukas Brothers|website=BestNewYorkComedy.com |date=July 8, 2012|access-date=October 12, 2013}}</ref> Mantzoukas continued to write and perform as a duo with [[Jessica St. Clair]] appearing in the sketch show, "We Used to Go Out" and long-form improv show, "First Date".<ref name="jester"/><ref>{{cite news |first=Jason |last=Zinoman |title=Being in Love Is Impossible, but Being Alone Is Even Worse |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/03/08/theater/reviews/being-in-love-is-impossible-but-being-alone-is-even-worse.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=March 8, 2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Review: We Used to Go Out |url=https://ucbcomedy.com/media/5880 |work=UCB Comedy }}</ref> Together, he and St. Clair pitched a pilot to [[HBO]] (which was ultimately not picked up) and earned a deal with [[Comedy Central]].<ref name="jester"/> The two were compared to [[Nichols and May]], and continue to collaborate and perform on the podcast ''[[Womp It Up!]]''.<ref>{{cite web |first=Jesse David |last=Fox |title=Talking with Jessica St. Clair & Lennon Parham About Best Friends Forever |url=https://www.vulture.com/2012/04/talking-with-jessica-st-clair-lennon-parham-about-best-friends-forever.html |work=[[New York (magazine)#Digital expansion and destination sites|Vulture]] |date= April 25, 2012}}</ref> Mantzoukas taught advanced improv classes at UCB.<ref>{{cite web|title= Jason Mantzoukas: 'Improv is Funny, But it Doesn't Have to Be' |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0VWg3ldzbLo |work=The Off Camera Show |date=May 16, 2019}}</ref>

Bang! (TV series)|Comedy Bang! Bang!]]'', ''[[Transparent (TV series)|Transparent]]'', ''[[Brooklyn Nine-Nine]]'', ''[[I'm Sorry (TV series)|I'm Sorry]]'', and ''[[The Good Place]]''.<ref name="Offer inter" /><ref name="IMDb">{{cite web|title=Jason Mantzoukas – IMDb|url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1727621/?ref_=ttfc_fc_cl_t20|work=[[IMDb]]}}</ref>

Mantzoukas has done voice acting work, including main roles on the animated series ''[[Big Mouth (American TV series)|Big Mouth]]'', ''[[Close Enough]]'', ''[[HouseBroken]]'', and ''[[Star Trek: Prodigy]]''.<ref name="IMDb" /> In 2018, he replaced [[T.J. ===Writing===
In 2008, [[NBC]] ordered a [[Television pilot|pilot]] for a comedy series written by Mantzoukas called ''Off Duty''.<ref name="Offer inter"/><ref>{{cite news |first=Nellie |last= Andreeva |title=Comedy duo goes 'Off Duty' |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/comedy-duo-goes-duty-114956 |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=July 1, 2008}}</ref> The pilot was filmed in New York starring [[Bradley Whitford]] and [[Romany Malco]] but the series was not picked up.<ref name="Offer inter"/> In interviews in 2014, Mantzoukas announced that he was working on a "loosely autobiographical" television show for [[Showtime (TV network)|Showtime]] about life after ending a long-term relationship.<ref name="Offer inter"/>

Mantzoukas earned credit for writing the screenplay draft of the [[Buddy cop film|buddy cop]] comedy ''[[Ride Along (film)|Ride Along]]'', starring [[Ice Cube]] and [[Kevin Hart]].<ref name=THR-Cube>{{cite news |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |title=Ice Cube film, Fox comedy on scribe's plate |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/ice-cube-film-fox-comedy-91783 |work= [[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=November 29, 2009}}</ref> He originally was asked to write for [[Andy Samberg]] as one of the leads, but the rights to the film were ultimately purchased by [[Universal Pictures|Universal Studios]] who later cast Hart in the role originally intended for Samberg.<ref>{{cite podcast |url=https://armchairexpertpod.com/pods/jason-mantzoukas |title=Jason Mantzoukas |website=[[Armchair Expert]] |publisher=[[Stitcher Radio]] |host=[[Dax Shepard]], Monica Padman |date=February 11, 2019 |time=1:18:05}}</ref> He has served as a consulting writer and producer on ''[[Childrens Hospital]]'' and ''[[Portlandia (TV series)|Portlandia]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sfsketchfest.com/x/performers/jason-mantzoukas/| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140226190100/http://sfsketchfest.com/x/performers/jason-mantzoukas/|title=Jason Mantzoukas|website=[[SF Sketchfest]]|year=2012|archive-date=February 26, 2014}}</ref>

==Personal life==
As of 2015, he was living in [[Los Angeles]].<ref name="Website-1">{{Cite web |last=Only |first=Subscription |date=2015-09-09 |title=League Star Jason Mantzoukas Shares His Favorite Podcasts and Why He’s Not on Social Media |url=https://www.adweek.com/brand-marketing/league-star-jason-mantzoukas-shares-his-favorite-podcasts-and-why-he-s-not-social-media-166713/ |access-date=2026-10-17 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Mantzoukas does not use social media, saying in 2015: "From the very beginning, when IM-ing first became a thing, I was like, "Why? What's this about?" They just didn't interest me. I completely understand social media as a method of promotion and digesting information, but it just seems like a colossal waste of time to me, and there's a million other ways I'd rather waste my time."<ref name="Website-1" /> However, he will browse sites like [[Twitter]] if "something is blowing up or somebody posts a picture that everyone is talking about, then I'll go look at it."<ref name="Website-1" />

Mantzoukas was born with an [[egg allergy]] and experiences [[anaphylaxis]] if he ingests eggs.<ref name="eggs">{{cite news|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/entertainment/movies/ct-ent-my-worst-moment-jason-mantzoukas-1114-story.html| first=Nina|last=Metz|title=My Worst Moment: Jason Mantzoukas and the dangerous granola|date=November 13, 2018|access-date=December 17, 2018|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]}}</ref> He has cited this allergy as the cause of his [[hypochondria]]c tendencies.<ref>{{cite podcast |url=https://armchairexpertpod.com/pods/jason-mantzoukas |title=Jason Mantzoukas |website=[[Armchair Expert]] |publisher=[[Stitcher Radio]] |host=[[Dax Shepard]], Monica Padman |date=February 11, 2019 |time=23:37}}</ref>

He was previously in a relationship with actress [[Connie Britton]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.redbookmag.com/life/interviews/a5230/connie-britton-interview-2009/ |first=Margot |last=Dougherty |title=Connie Britton: What 40 Feels Like |date=September 15, 2009 |work=[[Redbook]] |quote= I have a great man in my life — he's a comedy writer [Jason Mantzoukas], but I probably shouldn't say much more than that! — but that's awesome. And that happened after I turned 40.}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/annehelenpetersen/the-cult-of-connie-britton |first=Anne Helen |last=Petersen|title=The Cult of Connie Britton |date=November 9, 2014 |work=[[BuzzFeed]] |quote=...Britton's been linked with comedian Jason Mantzoukas...}}</ref>

{{Short description|American actress and dancer (1964–2020)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=July 2020}} {{Infobox person | name = Galyn Görg | image = Morta-Galyn-Gorg-Fantastico_resize.jpg | caption = | other_names = Galyn Gorg
Galan Gorg
Gaylyn Görg | birth_date = {{birth date|1964|7|15}} | birth_place = [[Los Angeles|Los Angeles, California]], U.S. | death_date = {{death date and given age|2020|7|14|55}} | death_place = [[Hawaii]], U.S. | death_cause = | occupation = {{hlist|Actress|dancer}} | years_active = 1983–2020 }} '''Galyn Görg'''{{efn|{{IPAc-en|ˈ|g|eɪ|l|ɪ|n|_|ˈ|dʒ|ɔː|r|dʒ}} {{respell|GAY|lin|_|JORJ}}; last name pronounced as though spelled ''George''}}{{efn|Also credited as '''Galyn Gorg''', '''Galan Gorg''' and '''Gaylyn Görg'''}} (July 15, 1964 – July 14, 2020) was an American actress and dancer, best known for her role in the film ''[[RoboCop 2]]'' as Angie, the villain Cain's girlfriend and subordinate; on ''[[M.A.N.T.I.S.]]'', television's first [[African-American|black]] superhero program, as Lt. Maxwell; on the television show ''[[Twin Peaks]]'' as Nancy O'Reilly;{{cite web|url=http://twinpeaksarchive.blogspot.com/2009/12/exclusive-galyn-gorg-interview.html|title=Exclusive Galyn Görg Interview!|work=Twin Peaks Archive|first=Jerry|last=Horne|date=August 27, 1994|access-date=November 29, 2013}} and as a starring dancer on two separate [[Italy|Italian]] variety shows, ''[[Fantastico (variety show)|Fantastico]]'' on the channel ''[[RAI]]'' and ''[[:it:SandraRaimondo Show|SandraRaimondo Show]]'' on the channel ''[[Canale 5]]''. ==Early life== Görg was born in [[Los Angeles|Los Angeles, California]] to an actress/model mother of [[African Americans|African American]], [[Choctaw people|Choctaw]], [[Blackfoot people|Blackfoot]], and [[Irish people|Irish]] descent, and a documentary filmmaker father of [[Germans|German]] descent. She was raised in [[Hawaii]] and majored in liberal arts at [[Santa Monica City College]].{{cite web|url=http://www.xenaville.com/cast/gorg.html|title=Galyn Gorg|work=Xenaville|access-date=November 29, 2013}} ==Career== Görg's career began with dancing. Trained in jazz, ballet, Haitian, Afro-Samba, Afro-Cuban, West African, hip-hop, hula and funk, she trained with the [[Roland Dupree Dance Academy]] and the [[Alvin Ailey]] Summer Program, and went on to work with choreographers such as [[Debbie Allen]], [[Michael Peters (choreographer)|Michael Peters]], and [[Marguerite Derricks]]. She studied acting with, among other groups, Improv for the People, [[The Groundlings]], and the Pacific Resident Theater.{{cite web|url=http://www.pdf.investintech.com/preview/8ebc3cec-c684-11e4-b21a-002590d31986/index.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20150310010404/http://www.pdf.investintech.com/preview/8ebc3cec-c684-11e4-b21a-002590d31986/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 10, 2015|work=Galyn Görg|title=Biography|date=January 10, 2015|access-date=July 15, 2020}} Görg's work in film, television, music videos and live theatrical performances spanned a multitude of countries, including the [[Middle East]], [[Italy]], [[Mexico]], [[New Zealand]], [[Canada]] and other parts of the world. She starred as the love-interest dancer in the iconic [[ZZ Top]] music video "[[Sharp Dressed Man]]" and achieved fame in Italy as the dance star of two variety series on Italian television: ''[[Fantastico (variety show)|Fantastico]]'' (on ''[[RAI]]'') and ''[[:it:SandraRaimondo Show|SandraRaimondo Show]]'' (on ''[[Canale 5]]''). Görg's best-known role was Lt. Leora Maxwell in the 1994 TV series ''[[M.A.N.T.I.S.]]'', which was adapted from a film of the same name. The character played by Görg was not present in the film/pilot of the television show, but was added when the show was picked up by [[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox Network]]. There was controversy surrounding the series at the time due to accusations that the producers removed [[African-American]] themes to make it more appealing to mainstream viewers.{{cite web|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/1994/08/27/mantis-producers-dispute-claims-theyve-lightenedup-the-new-fox-series/|title='M.A.N.T.I.S.' producers dispute claims they've 'lightened' up the new Fox series|work=The Baltimore Sun|first=Greg|last=Braxton|date=August 27, 1994|access-date=November 29, 2013|archive-date=December 3, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203033500/http://articles.baltimoresun.com/1994-08-27/features/1994239090_1_mantis-galyn-gorg-gina-torres|url-status=live}} ==Personal life and death== Görg was also a professional dancer who lectured at schools and performed all over the world.{{cite web|url=http://wp1.dreamshapers.info/galyn-gorg|title=Galyn Görg profile|work=Dream Shapers|access-date=November 29, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203021347/http://wp1.dreamshapers.info/galyn-gorg|archive-date=December 3, 2013}} She died of cancer on July 14, 2020, a day before her 56th birthday. She was diagnosed the week before, after doctors found cancer throughout her body and lungs.{{cite web|url=https://heavy.com/entertainment/2020/07/galyn-gorg-dead|title='Robocop 2' & 'The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air' Star Galyn Gorg Dies at 55|first=Paul|last=Farrell|date=July 15, 2020|website=[[Heavy.com]]|access-date=July 15, 2020|archive-date=July 15, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200715224011/https://heavy.com/entertainment/2020/07/galyn-gorg-dead/|url-status=dead}} Görg never married and had no children.{{cite web|url= https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/galyn-gorg-dead-twin-peaks-fresh-prince-bel-air-actress-was-55-1303467|title=Galyn Görg, Actress on ‘Twin Peaks’ and ‘Fresh Prince of Bel-Air,’ Dies at 55|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|publisher=[[Eldridge Industries]]|last=Barnes|first=Mike|date=July 16, 2020|accessdate=July 18, 2026}} ==Filmography== ===Film=== {| class="wikitable sortable" ! {{short description|American actor (1946–2022)}} {{Infobox person |name = Danny Goldring |image = Danny Goldring in Bean.png |caption = Goldring as Security Buck in ''[[Bean (film)|Bean]]'' (1997) |birth_date = {{Birth date|1946|5|31}} |birth_place = [[Woodstock, Illinois]], U.S. |death_date = {{Death date and age|2022|12|2|1946|5|31}} |death_place = [[Los Angeles, California]], U.S. |occupation = Actor |education = [[Trinity University (Texas)|Trinity University]] }} '''Danny Goldring''' (May 31, 1946 – December 2, 2022) was an American actor.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/232272378/|title=Unmasking Chicago actor Danny Goldring|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|location=[[Chicago, Illinois]]|date=July 18, 2008|access-date=April 3, 2022|pages=5–9|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Closed access}} He was best known for playing and Tom Kane's childhood friend Ryan Kavanaugh in the American [[political drama]] television series ''[[Boss (TV series)|Boss]]''.{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2012/09/28/danny-goldrings-long-chicago-acting-career-paying-off-with-boss/|title=Danny Goldring's long Chicago acting career paying off with 'Boss'|first=Rick|last=Kogan|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=September 28, 2012|access-date=April 3, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150107105512/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2012-09-28/entertainment/ct-ae-0930-kogan-sidewalks-20120929_1_tom-kane-danny-goldring-fictional-mayor|archive-date=January 7, 2015|url-status=live|via=[[Wayback Machine]]}} == Life and career == Goldring was born in [[Woodstock, Illinois]], the son of a [[United States Navy]] [[Personnel of the United States Navy|officer]]. He attended a [[College-preparatory school|preparatory school]] in [[Maryland]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98618013/thank-lunching-for-launching-a/|title=Thank 'Lunching' for launching a revitalized Danny Goldring|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|location=[[Chicago, Illinois]]|date=March 31, 1978|access-date=April 3, 2022|page=18|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}} Goldring then attended [[Trinity University (Texas)|Trinity University]]. At the age of 18, while Goldring was visiting some friends of his in [[New York (state)|New York]], it was suggested to him that he should become an actor. Goldring served in the [[Signal Corps (United States Army)|Signal Corps]] branch of the [[United States Army]]. After being discharged, he worked in construction in Maryland, where he made his stage debut in a production of ''[[A Thurber Carnival]]''. Goldring worked as a [[Puppetry|puppeteer]] with the [[Cole Marionettes]], with whom he toured for two years. Goldring returned to [[Chicago|Chicago, Illinois]], in 1970. He attended [[The Theatre School at DePaul University]], where he appeared in the stage play ''[[One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest (play)|One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest]]''. After leaving in 1973 he appeared in various [[radio]] and stage plays in Chicago. Goldring began appearing in film and television in 1976, his first role being in the television film ''The Last Affair''. He then appeared in the television [[soap opera]] ''[[Search for Tomorrow]]'', playing Beau Mitchell. Goldring also played Hank in ''[[Texas (TV series)|Texas]]''. He has guest-starred in various television programs including ''[[ER (TV series)|ER]]'', ''[[Matlock (1986 TV series)|Matlock]]'', ''[[Star Trek: Deep Space Nine]]'', ''[[Star Trek: Voyager]]'', ''[[Star Trek: Enterprise]]'', ''[[NYPD Blue]]'', ''[[Early Edition]]'', ''[[Wings (1990 TV series)|Wings]]'' and ''[[The Practice]]''. Goldring played the role of [[Major League Baseball|Major League baseball]] [[catcher]] and manager "[[Bill Carrigan]]" in the 1992 film ''[[The Babe]]''.{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=iZQ-amN0wTkC|title=Screen World 1993: Comprehensive Pictorial and Statistical Record of the 1992 Movie Season|page=51|first=John|last=Willis|publisher=Hal Leonard Corporation|date=February 2000|isbn=9781557831750|via=[[Google Books]]}} He co-starred and appeared in major films such as ''[[The Dark Knight]]'' (as masked bank robber "Grumpy"), ''[[Bean (film)|Bean]]'', ''[[Chicago Overcoat]]'', ''[[Chain Reaction (1996 film)|Chain Reaction]]'' and ''[[The Fugitive (1993 film)|The Fugitive]]''. In 2014, Goldring starred in the film ''[[Dig Two Graves]]'', where he played Proctor.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/03/23/movies/dig-two-graves-review.html|title=Review: 'Dig Two Graves,' but the Goodbye Is Only Temporary|first=Andy|last=Webster|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=March 23, 2017|access-date=April 3, 2022}} On stage, he played Detective Vince Getz in ''Big Lake Big City'' at the [[Lookingglass Theatre Company]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.theatreinchicago.com/news.php?articleID=740|title=Bad Cops Finish First: Danny Goldring Plays All Sides of the Law|work=Theatre in Chicago|first=Mary|last=Shen Barnidge|date=2013|access-date=April 3, 2022}} His most recent role was in [[Adult Swim]]'s ''[[Joe Pera Talks with You]]'', where he played Grandpa 'Papa' Joe.{{citation needed|date=November 2022}} Goldring died on December 2, 2022, at the age of 76.{{Cite web|url=https://chicagoreader.com/arts-culture/performing-arts-feature/remembering-danny-goldring/|title=Remembering Danny Goldring|work=[[Chicago Reader]]|date=December 12, 2022}} == Filmography == === Film === {| class="wikitable sortable plainrowheaders" |+ {{Screen reader-only|Danny Goldring' film credits}} |- !
